title: perf(ui): build the stock eye on a worker thread at start
body:
`StockEye::new` took about 430 ms on the UI thread before the first frame. It now runs on a worker thread. The shell takes the eye on a later frame, as the browser shell does. Until then the viewport draws the stock sheet.

Readings (Windows 11, DX12, release): the window first answers at 730/806/1079 ms before and 344/369/448 ms after.

## Testing
`cargo xtask gate quick --base main` on this head: the 8 integration suites passed in every run. The `ui build (--no-run)` step and `ui suites: lib` were red in some runs:
- Default jobs (16), after a clean build: the build step failed with "invalid metadata files" errors for a dependency crate. The lib step passed in that run.
- 4 jobs (`CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=4`): the build step passed. `ui suites: lib` ended with STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION.

The STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION is not from this PR. It also happens on plain `main`: 8 of 15 runs of `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` on Windows 11 ended with it. On this branch, 2 of 10 runs did. It stops at a random test each time. So the full lib step is not shown green on this head by the gate. Earlier, 1479 lib tests passed in 4 other plain `cargo test` runs on this branch.

Run by name with `cargo xtask gate test <name> --crate camcraft-ui --exact`, all ok:
- `nothing_yet_keeps_the_receiver`
- `a_refusal_is_handed_over_once`
- `a_thread_that_ended_without_a_result_is_named`
- `the_eye_can_cross_threads` (`StockEye` is `Send`)

Not exercised: clippy (not installed here), macOS, Linux, the other gate tiers, the traced-stock view on the first frames (not looked at by eye), closing the window while the eye is still building.

Changelog: The window answers sooner after start.
Refs #3583

title: feat(ui): add --no-activate and --minimized start options
body:
Adds two start options. `--no-activate` creates the window inactive and skips `focus_window()`. `--minimized` also minimizes the window at once.

Cause: winit shows a visible, active window with `SW_SHOW`, and the shell called `focus_window()`.

Readings (Windows 11, release build, polled with EnumWindows/GetForegroundWindow, launched from a terminal and from Task Scheduler):
- `--no-activate`: never the foreground window, also when the project finished loading.
- `--minimized`: minimized (`IsIconic`) from the first time it is visible; never the foreground window.

## Testing
`cargo xtask gate quick --base main` on this head, with `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=4`: 10 steps, 0 failed. `ui suites: lib`: 1479 passed. The 8 integration suites passed.

Run by name with `cargo xtask gate test <name> --crate camcraft-ui --exact`, all ok:
- `start_mode_flags_are_read_and_minimized_implies_no_activate`
- `default_start_activates_and_shows`
- `no_activate_shows_without_the_focus`
- `minimized_creates_an_inactive_window`
- `each_table_option_is_accepted_by_the_parser`
- `help_names_each_option_and_variable_of_the_table`

Two runs with the default job count (16) were red:
- The `ui build (--no-run)` step failed with "found invalid metadata files" for a dependency crate (`png`, then `accesskit`). This looks like a build-cache problem on this machine. It did not repeat with 4 jobs.
- `ui suites: lib` ended with STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION. This crash also happens on plain `main`, without this PR: 8 of 15 runs of `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` on Windows 11 ended with it. It stops at a random test each time. This PR does not cause it. The one run with 4 jobs did not crash, so a full green lib run is one sample only.

Not exercised: clippy (not installed here), macOS, Linux (Wayland ignores `with_active`), the other gate tiers.

Changelog: Start options `--no-activate` and `--minimized` open the window without taking the focus.
Fixes #3582

title: fix(2d): note the corner reliefs that get no spur
body:
## What changed

A planned corner relief whose start no pass vertex reaches, and for which no legal detour exists, was dropped without a diagnostic (#3249). It could leave material the operator does not expect.

- `inject_relief_spurs` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/corner_relief_spur.rs`) now reports each skipped relief: the caller gets the relief start points in a `misses` vector.
- The pocket emit path (`pocket_emit.rs`) and the pocket avoid path (`pocket_avoid.rs`) write one note per corner into the `PathBuilder` / path notes: `corner relief at (x, y) is not cut: no pass vertex reaches the relief spur`. Notes are de-duplicated by corner, so a multi-level cut or a retry names each corner once.
- The four-dogbones rest test keeps its no-note assert: a reached relief adds no note.

Changelog: A 2D Pocket corner relief that no pass reaches is now named in the operation notes instead of being dropped silently.

## Pinning tests

- `machining2d::corner_relief_spur::tests::a_relief_no_pass_reaches_is_reported_as_a_miss` (crates/motion/src/machining2d/corner_relief_spur.rs): the miss is reported and no spur is spliced in; a reached relief reports no miss and gets its spur.
- `unreachable_corners_and_bad_overrides_are_refused` (crates/motion/tests/corner_relief.rs): the island-blocked spur refuses at plan time.
- `crates/motion/tests/rest_corner_relief.rs`: the rest pass keeps its no-note assert.

## Not exercised

- The note text in a posted NC program through the full post pipeline.
- The avoid-path note on a multi-level cut with more than one skipped corner.

Fixes #3249

title: fix(2d): enter a dead-end later Outside pass by a ramp along the pass
body:
A dead-end later Outside pass now enters by a ramp along the pass, so the later pass starts in cleared stock.

## What changed

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/level_order.rs`: `lead_in` searched only 0.9 tool radii. Each later pass starts at a dead end one stepover (4.00 mm) from the nearest cut walk. The new entry ramps along the pass at a dead end, at 3 degrees.
- The incompleteness guard (`unswept`, `LEFT_TOL` 0.1 mm2) and the `RINGS_FALLBACK` warning stay. No refusal is changed. The removed `PassStart::rank` and the parallel `sided_rings` planner are not re-added.

## The pin

`outside_entries_after_the_first_land_in_cleared_stock` (100 x 40 band, radius 15, 2D Offset Outside, 0.25 mm material grid, 3 tool radii of floor feed after the first land):

- Red on main `4c0a157e1`: 332.88 mm2 of uncut stock.
- Green on this head: 0.00 mm2.

## Readings

`CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=3`, `-j 3`, no sccache:

- motion `pass_start_engagement`, `pass_start_levels`, and the lib `machining2d` tests: green.
- app `offset_pass_start` and app `example_catalog`: green.
- motion clippy: clean.
- The full `cargo xtask gate quick` was stopped at the tier change and has no final verdict.

## Tier note

The fix came from an `issue-worker-high` worker while the issue was claimed at `effort:max` (the claim predates the label change). The claim of the earlier `issue-worker-max` worker is released: its worktree and its commit are gone. The surviving fix is branch `issue/3567-ramp-entry-at-dead-end` at `e7ae538a3`. The review runs at the `effort:max` tier.

Changelog: 2D Offset Outside: a later pass that starts at a dead end now enters by a 3-degree ramp along the pass, so the entry starts in cleared stock and leaves no uncut band.

Fixes #3567

body:
## What changed

The quick plan now selects the app suites that post the shipped examples. The trigger is a diff that touches one of these paths:

- `assets/posts/` (a `.cps` post script)
- `assets/machines/`
- `examples/` (also `examples/catalog/**`)
- `crates/post/src/` and `crates/motion/src/` (the post and toolpath engines; this fits as two entries of the same table, so no redesign)

The new rule is in `xtask/src/example_suites.rs` (`INPUTS`, `SUITES`, `map`). `quick.rs` calls it in place of `catalog::map_catalog`. `map` calls `map_catalog` first, so the catalog reason of #2393 stays. The heavy reach (`heavy.rs`) does not change.

Selected app suites (`app suites: <name>`, each only if the binary exists):

- `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`, `first_part_programs` (the issue)
- `first_router_part` (posts `examples/first-router-part.camproj`)
- `first_4axis_part`, `continuous_4axis_part`, `tilt_basis_compat` (compare a shipped `.nc`)
- `catalog_groove_part_off` (reads a posted catalog case)

Not added: `agie_native` (it reads `examples/agie` only as input). The UI suites `catalog_render`, `egui_app` and `gpu_render` render example projects but post nothing. The decision is in `docs/decisions/3521-gate-selects-example-posts.md`.

The gate skill (`.claude/skills/gate/SKILL.md`, "What quick selects") has a new item for the rule. `AGENTS.md` is not changed: "Heavy lanes at review" stays true.

## Dry run: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main --dry-run`, scratch change to `assets/posts/grblhal.cps`

- Before (origin/main 16dc39f06): 57 steps. No `example_catalog*` step, no `first_part_programs` step. Only `first_router_part` (it names `grblhal.cps`).
- After: 66 steps. New steps: `app suites: catalog_groove_part_off`, `continuous_4axis_part`, `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`, `first_4axis_part`, `first_part_programs`, `tilt_basis_compat`. body:
Ports three engagement pins from PR #3439 onto main's Pass start law
(`crates/motion/src/machining2d/level_rings.rs` and `level_order.rs`).
The change is test-only. It changes no product code.

## What is ported

- `outside_on_a_figure_eight_band_never_slots`: Outside on a synthetic
  figure-eight band cuts no wider than 1.5 stepovers over any 3 tool
  radii of floor feed. Main pins this law only in the ignored heavy app
  test `fig8_outside_offset_cuts_no_move_at_full_width`. This pin gives
  default-suite coverage.
- `inside_on_the_band_clears_the_whole_band`: Inside on the round-part
  band leaves less than 0.5 mm2 of stock off the part wall. It checks
  both climb directions.
- `auto_on_the_band_slots_so_the_measure_sees_a_slot`: Auto (core first)
  on the same band slots. This pin is the positive control for the width
  measure.

## Readings

| Test | Result | Time |
|---|---|---|
| outside_on_a_figure_eight_band_never_slots | pass | 0.94 s |
| inside_on_the_band_clears_the_whole_band | pass | 2.08 s |

title: refactor(multiaxis): split first_traverse.rs along the domain seam
body:
refactor(multiaxis): split first_traverse.rs along the domain seam

## What moved where and why

`crates/app/src/operation/first_traverse.rs` was 432 lines, over the
400-line limit. The file held two concerns. The split follows the seam:

- `first_traverse.rs` (now 320 lines) keeps the seam to the
  first-traverse laws: which operations answer to them (`answers`,
  `mill_order`, `newly_judged`, `newly_judged_on`), what they read over
  (`Over`, `Turned`, `rides_of`, `rotaries_of`, `turned_axis`), the
  rotary swept law (`judge_turned`), the verdict choreography (`judge`)
  and the user-heights framing (`in_user_frame`).
- `first_traverse_table.rs` (new, 131 lines) holds the 3+2 tilted-table
  reading (#2987, #3081): `tilting_all`, `work_tilts`,
  `table_top_face`, `TableRead`, `table_read`, `TABLE_UNJUDGED_NOTE`,
  and the catalog table test. It has a one-line provenance comment.

The moved items are re-exported from `first_traverse`
(`pub(super) use`), so every caller - `generate.rs`, `stamp.rs`,
`rotary_traverse.rs`, `first_traverse_posed.rs` - keeps its paths and
the public API is stable. `operation/mod.rs` registers the new module.

## Test count

`#[test]` count in `crates/app` (src + tests): 4324 before, 4324 after.
The catalog table test moved with its code into the new module; no
coverage rode the split away.

## Gate results

`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` on the final head: green.
The touched suites include `app:lib`, `app:first_traverse`,
`app:first_traverse_table_tilt`, `app:first_traverse_posed`,
`app:first_traverse_rotary`, `app:first_traverse_rotary_mill_turn`,
`app:first_traverse_mill_turn` and the `camcraft-ui` suites that the
gate map reaches - all pass. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app
--all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised

No behaviour change is intended or exercised: this is a code move.
No heavy lane is reached by a pure move inside `crates/app/src/operation`.

title: feat(app): add built-in 3D multi-setup simulation video renderer
body:
CamCraft should support exporting a simulation movie showing how material was removed from stock.  This can be used by users to validate that the machining process makes sense.  It should be supported in headless mode so that it can be used during batch processing of a large number of machining jobs.

This pull request adds a  a pure-Rust, headless 3D material-removal simulation movie renderer to `camcraft-app` exposed consistently through the CLI (`camcraft-cli render-video`), the MCP JSON-RPC server (`render_simulation_video`), and Boa JS job scripts (`cam.call("render_simulation_video", {...})`).

[![Example video export](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e508d989-ce43-4d53-911a-d91e73997d2a)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e508d989-ce43-4d53-911a-d91e73997d2a)


### Design
 
------
- `crates/app/src/sim_video/` (zero new external crate dependencies):
  - `math.rs`: `Vec3`, `Mat3` (`from_quat` matching `camcraft-geometry` `[x, y, z, w]` layout), shortest-arc `quat_slerp` with double-cover sign handling, pinhole `Camera`, slab AABB intersection, and analytic ray-cylinder / ray-cone / ray-sphere intersections for tool rendering.
  - `voxel.rs`: persistent single-byte 3D voxel billet (`VoxelStock`) held in document/part frame with per-surface operation color tags (`TAG_*`), fast column-bound carving along `±Z` (`col_max_z`/`col_min_z`), general arbitrary-axis carving (`carve_oriented`) for side-on and tilted 5-axis moves, `mask_cylinder_z`, watertight `mask_mesh` ray-parity masking, 3x3x3 occupancy gradient normals, and neighborhood ambient occlusion.
  - `plan.rs`: extracts generated setups, `setup_align::stored` inverse rigid alignments, WCS labels (`G54`..`G59`/`G54.1P*`) and origins, `StockShape::{Box, Cylinder, FromModel}`, tool shapes (`Flat`, `Ball`, `Bull`, `Drill`, `Chamfer`), chord-tessellated `Move::segments3` arcs, optional 5-axis tilted `Move.axis`, and part mesh volume across aligned setups.
  - `render.rs`: `rayon`-parallel 3D DDA ray-marcher (Amanatides-Woo) with studio floor grid & drop shadow, Blinn-Phong metallic shading, contact cutting glow, spinning fluted analytic cutters/shanks/holders, and a depth-tested live 3D toolpath ribbon trail (blue feed, amber plunge, red rapid).
  - `hud.rs`: clean-room 5x7 ASCII bitmap font rendering the setup/op top bar, tool/RPM/feed badge, WCS DRO readout, volume tracker, `M0 STOP` transition banners, and segmented operation progress bar with responsive layout clamping for narrow resolutions (e.g. 640x360).
  - `encode.rs`: dual frame sinks supporting pure-Rust RGB8 PNG frame sequences (`format = "frames"`, zero external tools required) and raw RGB24 streaming to `ffmpeg` for `.mp4` (`libx264`), `.webm` (`libvpx`), and `.gif` (two-pass palette filter).
  - `mod.rs`: orchestrator with proportional `sqrt(len)` op frame budgeting, quaternion SLERP setup re-orientation animations, auto-azimuth framing for asymmetric side-turned setups (`setup_az_bias`), single-pass frame teeing for `--per-setup` split videos, silent prior-setup carry replay for `--setup <name>`, turntable showcase spin (with upright return for side-turned final setups), optional PNG keyframe capture, and explicit validation/refusal checks (resolution bounds, even dimensions for `yuv420p` mp4/webm, `fps`, `cell_mm`, 120M voxel cap).
- Wiring & safety gates:
  - `crates/app/src/mcp/video.rs` & `mcp/tools.rs`: registers `render_simulation_video` (schema with `additionalProperties: false`).
  - `crates/app/src/mcp/live.rs`: gates `render_simulation_video` under `GateKind::FileWrite` for live GUI MCP approval parity (#1942).
  - `crates/app/src/cli_video.rs` & `cli.rs`: adds `camcraft-cli render-video` to `TOP_USAGE` and `HELP_LANES` (thin wrapper generating `cam.load` / optional `cam.generate` / `cam.call("render_simulation_video", ...)`).
  - Regenerated `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` (`117 -> 118` tools) and updated `site/content/guide/automate/mcp.md`.

Testing
-------
- New internal unit test suite `crates/app/src/sim_video/tests.rs` (16 tests):
  New integration test suite `crates/app/tests/sim_video.rs` (8 hermetic tests using pure-Rust `format = "frames"`, zero `ffmpeg` required):
  - Single-setup render + `cam.call` JS bridge & PNG header verification.
  - 3-setup upright (`G54`) / 180° flip / -90° side-on render via MCP `tools/call`, checking monotonic volume reduction, part mesh volume across aligned setups, `--per-setup` directory PNG counts matching report, keyframes, and `--setup` filter silent carry parity.
- Rendered real outputs end-to-end with release `camcraft-cli render-video`:
  - 3-setup double-ear clevis bracket (`960x540`, `30 fps`, `0.25 mm` voxel pitch, `424x288x288` grid, `--per-setup`): 1,221 frames + 3 split MP4s + 20 PNG keyframes in 24.9s (`549.5 -> 133.7 cm^3` vs `129.5 cm^3` CAD).
  - `examples/first-part.camproj` (`--generate`, `.webm` & `640x360` PNG frames): `120.0 -> 67.95 cm^3` vs `67.36 cm^3` CAD.

title: docs(process): targeted tests at review, the full heavy lanes at the cut
body:
Maintainer decision (question dialog, 2026-11-22): "Targeted tests, heavy at the cut"

This PR changes the process texts to the six points of the decision on #3556 and #2568. It changes no code.

## What changed

- `AGENTS.md`
  - "Heavy lanes at review": a review needs the pinning tests, the touched test binaries (the quick plan), the example catalog suites by name where a post or a toolpath changed, and the light lane. No PR gets the full heavy lanes. A diff that reaches a heavy lane is not "not ready" for that reason. No PR is "owed heavy". The full heavy lanes run only at the cut, in the cut gate on the cut runner. A `P1` PR under the safety floor gets one targeted heavy step (`cargo xtask gate heavy --only "<crate> heavy: <target>"`). `P2` and lower get none. `cargo xtask gate heavy` and `--covers` stay as tools. They are not a condition for "ready" or for a merge. The sentence "the release tier at the cut stays the final check" stays.
  - **Owed heavy result** stays as a name, marked as retired, so that its citations resolve.
  - "The light lane": a red light run stays a note on the PR. It does not block the PR by itself. The full heavy steps of the red twins run at the cut, in the cut gate. A local run never replaces the cut gate.
  - The quick pass and "When PRs merge": a heavy lane result is not a condition, except the targeted step of a `P1` PR under the safety floor.
- `.claude/skills/gate/SKILL.md`: the heavy tier row, the heavy lane text, a new "targeted heavy step" item, the wave form as an optional tool, the owed rule marked as retired.
- `.claude/skills/work-issue/SKILL.md`: the worker names the review tests in the PR body. Only a `P1` PR under the safety floor runs the targeted heavy step.
- `.claude/skills/review-prs/SKILL.md`: step 2e is now "Targeted tests at review".
- `.claude/skills/merge-ready/SKILL.md`: step 4a is optional. The command and the `<!-- heavy-wave: ... -->` comment format stay. No merge waits for a record. Item 11 keeps one heavy condition: the targeted step of a `P1` PR under the safety floor.
- `.claude/agents/PR-reviewer.md`: step 5 runs the example catalog tests, the light lane, and the targeted heavy step for a `P1` PR under the safety floor only. The review comment lists those steps. "Not run" is never a pass for a required step.
- `docs/decisions/3556-targeted-tests-at-review.md`: the decision entry.

No change: `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`, `xtask/`, workflows, the known-fail marker rules, the cut rules, the pixel snapshot rules. `coordinator.md`, `issue-worker-*.md`, `gate-runner.md` and the `classify-effort` skill have no text that demands heavy lanes, so they do not change.

## Follow-up `c2dd094e9`

- The full heavy lanes run at the cut, in the cut gate on the cut runner, in all the process files. The earlier text named the post-merge runner. `.github/workflows/post-merge.yml` runs only the batch tier (`cargo xtask gate batch`), and the batch tier has no release heavy lanes. The decision file records that the maintainer's words named the post-merge runner, and why the text now names the cut gate.
- The light-lane rule drops the local rerun clause. The full heavy steps of the red twins run in the cut gate. They do not run locally before the cut.
- The xtask pin is renamed to `review_requires_targeted_heavy_tests_on_both_paths`. It pins the runner routing into step 5 for a `P1` targeted step. The `3460` decision cites the new name.

## Gate

Run on head `c2dd094e9`, with `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=3`:

- `cargo test -p xtask --bin xtask heavy_plan_tests`: 11 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p xtask --bin xtask light_tests`: 6 passed, 0 failed.
- `#[test]` count in `xtask/src/heavy_plan_tests.rs`: 11.
- Red on reverse: the routing pin fails when the runner-to-step-5 line is removed. The retired-demand pin fails when `report "heavy lanes not run" as a blocker` returns.

The quick plan selects `xtask unit tests` for this diff. The diff reaches no heavy lane.

## Open

1. Closed by `38eae631e`: the two xtask unit tests follow the new law. The renamed test `review_requires_targeted_heavy_tests_on_both_paths` pins the new law and the runner routing into step 5. The `#[test]` count stays 11.
2. "The touched test binaries (the quick plan)" when the quick plan falls back to the whole batch plan (a change in geometry, cl or a `Cargo.toml`): this PR does not decide it. See #3557.
3. Answered. The maintainer's comment on #3556 (2026-11-22, 19:37) says the full heavy steps of the red twins do not run locally before the cut. They run in the cut gate. `AGENTS.md` and the decision file now say this.
4. The targeted heavy step selects one heavy binary (`--only "<crate> heavy: <target>"`), not single test functions. The gate skill gives no form that runs one ignored test by name in release.
5. The heavy lock (decision point 5) is not in any process file. It is a local rule, so this PR adds no text for it.

Process change: yes

Changelog: none

title: fix(gpu): WGSL stock removal kernel for ball and flat on linear moves
body:
GPU stock sim S2 (#2627), a part of the fix of the slow stock simulation (#3336).

## What changed

- `crates/gpu/src/cut.wgsl` (new): the removal kernel. One workgroup (8 x 8) for each work item (one chord against one 8^3 brick). Each invocation cuts the eight z cells of one column. A claim folds into the lattice with `atomicMax` on the order-preserving u32 key of the S1 twin. Three entry points in one compute pass:
  - `cs_fill` writes the `-4 cap` floor key.
  - `cs_cut` claims.
  - `cs_decode` turns each key into the bits of its f32, in place. The buffer is then the f32 layer in the `pack_cut` layout (x fastest, then y, then z).
- `crates/gpu/src/cut.rs` (new): the plain-value input (`CutInput`, `CutGrid`, `CutItem`), its validation, and `cut_cpu`. `cut_cpu` copies the f32 twin of camcraft-sim operation for operation.
- `crates/gpu/src/cut_gpu.rs` (new): `CutKernel` (three pipelines, compiled one time for each device), the buffer plan against the device limits, at most 256 items in one dispatch of `cs_cut`, and a read-back with a time bound (`CUT_WAIT` = 10 s on the poll, 100 ms on the map callback).
- `crates/gpu/src/cut_run.rs` (new): the fallback rule `cut_or_cpu` / `cut_or_cpu_on`:
  - A missing device, a kernel error or a timeout gives the CPU law, with the reason logged one time.
  - Each GPU batch gets a spot check: up to 64 texels are compared with the CPU law. A GPU value more than half of the claim margin away rejects the batch.
  - A timeout or a failed spot check turns the GPU path off for the process.
- `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/cut_twin_work.rs`: the new `twin_items` gives the kernel items as plain numbers (`TwinItem`). `run_twin` now runs over those items. The result of `run_twin` does not change (the 7 old tests of `stock_cut_twin` stay green).
- `crates/sim/tests/stock_cut_twin.rs`: the new test `the_gpu_kernel_fixtures_match_the_twin` writes and checks `crates/gpu/tests/fixtures/cut_twin_{ball,flat}_2627.txt` (`CAMCRAFT_BLESS=1` writes them again, the `facet_grid_2619` pattern). Each fixture has the items, an FNV-1a hash of the twin layer, and the f64 layer (sparse). Sizes: 114 KB and 158 KB.
- `docs/decisions/2627-gpu-removal-kernel.md`: the decisions.

No new crate edge. `camcraft-gpu` keeps no `camcraft-*` dependency. The issue text asked for a `camcraft-gpu -> camcraft-sim` edge. The kernel needs only numbers, so the caller passes them in (decision file). No new external dependency. No change to `Cargo.toml` or `Cargo.lock`.

Display only: no verdict, post gate or posted G-code reads this kernel. `simulate_document` does not change.

## Readings (this machine, adapter "Microsoft Basic Render Driver" via Dx12, the software adapter)

Parity, f32 GPU against the f64 field cut (one-sided law of `stock_cut_twin::parity`, tolerance `96 * f32::EPSILON * 64 + 1e-4` = 8.3e-4, not changed):

| Batch | Items | GPU above f64 | Largest lag under f64 | max abs(GPU - CPU twin) | Smallest claim margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fixture, ball | 132 | never | 1.03e-4 | 0 (bit equal) | 4.9e-5 |
| fixture, flat | 224 | never | 1.54e-4 | 0 (bit equal) | 8.9e-5 |
| synthetic, ball (96x96x32) | 1536 | - | - | 0 (bit equal) | 1.1e-4 |
| synthetic, flat (96x96x32) | 1152 | - | - | 0 (bit equal) | 2.0e-4 |

Two runs on one device are bit equal. The CPU law in camcraft-gpu is bit equal to the sim twin (hash check).

Timings, release build, one batch (`cut_parity`, `--release`):

| Batch | GPU (software adapter) | CPU law (one thread) |
|---|---|---|
| synthetic ball, 1536 items, 166740 claimed texels | 20.3 ms | 17.5 ms |
| synthetic flat, 1152 items, 165415 claimed texels | 30.4 ms | 157.4 ms |
| fixture ball, 132 items | 11.9 ms | 1.1 ms |
| fixture flat, 224 items | 3.8 ms | 8.1 ms |

The kernel build (three pipelines) takes 4.2 ms. The GPU times include the upload, the three passes and the read-back.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/gpu/tests/cut_parity.rs` (6 tests):
  - `the_cpu_law_answers_the_sim_twin_bit_for_bit`
  - `the_gpu_cut_never_removes_more_than_the_f64_cut_when_an_adapter_exists`
  - `one_larger_batch_agrees_with_the_cpu_law_and_is_timed`
  - `no_device_falls_back_to_the_cpu_law_with_its_reason`
  - `a_layer_off_the_cpu_law_fails_the_spot_check`
  - `bad_input_refuses_by_name`
- `crates/sim/tests/stock_cut_twin.rs`: `the_gpu_kernel_fixtures_match_the_twin` (red first: the fixture did not exist, then blessed).

Without an adapter, the two GPU tests print `SKIPPED ... NOT a pass` and check that the CPU law answers. With `CAMCRAFT_REQUIRE_GPU=1` they fail. With `CAMCRAFT_GPU_COMPUTE=off` they skip by name (run: 6 passed). No test opens a window.

## Gate

Steps that I ran on head 5eb67ba20 (debug, `-j 6`):

- `gpu build`, `gpu suites: lib` (6), `bin_parity` (3), `cut_parity` (6), `refusals` (6): green.
- `sim build`, `sim suites: lib` and each sim integration suite of the quick plan, `stock_cut_twin` (8) included: green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-gpu -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Owed to the trial gate (in the quick plan, not run here by the instruction of the coordinator):

- `motion build`, `motion suites: lib`, `motion suites: posed_subtract`.
- `app build` and the 70 `app suites` steps of `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main --dry-run`.

Heavy lanes reached (`cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/main --dry-run`): `app heavy` (206 steps) and `motion heavy` (37 steps). Not run. "Not run" is not a pass.

## Not exercised

- A hardware adapter. `device_async` takes the software adapter first (#2621, item 4), so the readings are from WARP only. FMA contraction or a different `sqrt` on a hardware adapter can move the GPU value. The claim margin and the spot check are there for that case.
- The timeout path on a real hang (no test makes a device hang). The timeout text and the latch are in `cut_run.rs`.
- The viewport wiring. That is S3 (#2629). Two facts for S3 are on #2629:

- Extract per-level planning (`plan_avoid_level`), relief checks (`check_reliefs_avoid`), crossing-free checks (`enforce_level_crossing_free`), and rest dispatch (`emit_rest_avoid`) into `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket_avoid_level.rs`.
- Unify plain and rest avoid paths in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket_avoid.rs`, `rest2d.rs`, and `rest_prior.rs` under `pocket_avoid_over`.
- Check overhead keep-out zones up to `p.clearance_z.max(z)` so entry rapids and final clearance lifts clear overhead obstacles.
- Guard `Descent::Helix` (`m.solid_restart`) and `entry_restart` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/descent.rs` and `descent_dive.rs` with `helix_clears_prior`, `find_clear_helix_raw`, `moves_clear`, and `helix_cross_fallback`.
- Record between-pass `KeepDown` chords in `LinkState.level` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/ladder_links.rs`.
- Derive `Clone` for `LinkTally`, `LinkState`, and `WalkState`.
- Add pinning tests in `crates/motion/tests/avoid_pocket.rs`, `crates/app/tests/do_not_touch.rs`, and `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/do_not_touch.rs`.
- Record the design choice in `docs/decisions/3345-do-not-touch-2d-pocket.md`.

title: fix(project): save a project through a temp file and a rename
body:
## What changed

`project::save` now writes the project to a temporary file in the same
folder, flushes it, and renames it over the old file. It uses
`machine::store::write_atomic`, which machine files, preferences, recent
files and view settings already use. A failed save now keeps the old
project.

- Two refusals of the old plain write stay: a folder that does not exist,
  and a read-only project file. On Linux and macOS a rename replaces a
  read-only file, so `project::save` checks first.
- `machine::store::temp_path_for` gives the temp path. A path that names
  no file is now refused by name before a folder is made.
- The temp name has the process ID and a number for the calling thread.
  Before, two saves of one file at the same moment (an autosave and a
  save by the user) wrote the same temp file. Each thread takes its
  number one time, from one counter. The saves of one thread run one
  after another, so its name can repeat.
- No change to the file format, `PROJECT_VERSION` or the saved text.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/3509-atomic-project-save.md`.

This branch starts at upstream/main `dc86a8c48`.

## Tests

New in `crates/app/tests/project_roundtrip.rs`:

- `a_project_save_replaces_the_file_and_leaves_no_temp_file`
- `a_failed_project_save_keeps_the_old_file`
- `a_project_save_into_a_missing_folder_is_refused_and_makes_no_folder`
- `a_read_only_project_file_is_refused_and_kept`

New in `crates/app/tests/machine_edit.rs`:

- `two_threads_never_share_a_temp_file`

`cargo xtask gate quick` (Windows 11) on `dbe37ad2c`: green, 8 of 8 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled. The four new tests pass with the other 76 tests of `project_roundtrip`, and `two_threads_never_share_a_temp_file` passes with the other 12 tests of `machine_edit`. It ran the app unit
tests and the suites `contour_dxf_sketch`, `import_step_open_shell`,
`machine_edit`, `model_solid_ranges`, `project_roundtrip` and
`sketch_project`.
`cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
Heavy lanes: `cargo xtask gate heavy --dry-run` reaches every `app` heavy target (207 steps), because `crates/app/src` changed. I did not run them yet. I will run them on the final head before I mark this PR ready.

## Known limits

- A save over a project path that is a symbolic link replaces the link
  with a regular file. The target of the link does not change.
- The saved file gets the default permissions of a new file in that
  folder, not the permissions, owner or ACL of the old file. Machine
  files and preferences act the same way.

## Not exercised

- A real crash, full disk or lost network share during a write. The test
  with a folder in the place of the temp file makes the same failure path.
- A bare file name (`job.camproj`, no folder). Code inspection only: a
  test would change the current folder of the test process.
- Linux and macOS. The read-only check was run on Windows only.
- Two threads that save one file at the same moment. On Windows, two
  renames over one file at the same moment can fail for a reason that
  is not the temp name, so the test checks the temp names instead.

Changelog: Saving a project no longer destroys the old file when the write fails.
Effort: low

Fixes #3509

title: fix(sim): judge spot drill cones at the part top
body:
Stacked on #3472 (merge #3472 first)

## What changed

Judge an ordinary axial spot cone at the measured part top.
Use a separate optional `VerifyContext::rim_top_z` bound for finished hole walls.
Keep the stock top for rapid and collision checks.
Keep the nominal cutter radius for invalid caps, lateral feeds, and untrusted cutter geometry.
Other callers retain the stock-top fallback.

The synthetic case has a part top at Z12 and a stock top at Z13.
An 8 mm, 90-degree spot with its tip at Z10 now verifies and posts.
Its radius is 2 mm at the part top, inside the 2.5 mm hole radius.
A spot with its tip at Z9 still gives a gouge warning and blocks posting.

The gate also found one stale catalog assertion inherited from #3472.
Update its expected part-off Z from 13.5 to 12.
This matches the parent's corrected kerf and existing golden.
No golden file changes in this issue commit.

The decision record is `docs/decisions/3451-spot-drill-part-top.md`.

The #3020 cone check measured the radius at the raw stock top.

title: fix(turning): part-off states the piece kept and a back stock
body:
Stacked on #3472 (merge #3472 first). Before #3472 merges, this PR stays based on `main`; it carries the #3472 commits until then.

## What changed

The Part (part-off) operation gets one setting, `kerf: PartKerf` (`crates/motion/src/turning/parting_law.rs`). It has two values:

- `kept`: the piece that is the finished part.
  - `CutOff` (the default) is the #3452 rule. The whole kerf is on the chuck side.
  - `Chuck` keeps the piece in the chuck. The whole kerf is on the free-end side, and a stub comes off the free end.
- `back_stock` (mm, 0 or more, default 0): the whole kerf stands this far off the parting plane, into the scrap side. The part keeps that much on its end face for a later facing pass.

Where the setting is:

- Kernel: `part_in` reads the scrap side and the kerf flank from the setting.
- Gouge law: `part_kerf_refusal_for` judges the kerf against the part that `kept` names. It treats the back stock as part material. The old `part_kerf_refusal` calls it with the default.
- Flipped setup (`job.rs`): a setup that holds the part end for end refuses only the default now. The refusal names the setting: "Set 'The part is' to 'Chuck piece'". With `Chuck`, the part-off generates.
- Project file: the keys `kept` (`cut_off` / `chuck`) and `back_stock` (`project/part_kerf_dto.rs`). Each key is written only when it is not the default.
- Page: the Passes tab of the Part op has "The part is" (Cut-off piece / Chuck piece) and "Back stock". Apply rides `EditOperationParams`.
- MCP: `edit_operation` patches `kept` and `back_stock` through `EditOperationParams`. No new tool is necessary.
- Validation: a negative or non-finite back stock is refused at the command door (`is_sane`), in the kernel and in the verdict.
- Stamp: the setting is folded only when it is not the default. Thus no op saved before the setting reads stale.

The decision record: `docs/decisions/3469-part-kept-side.md`.

## Cause

#3472 put the whole kerf on the chuck side, and no parameter could change the side. In a flipped second setup the chuck holds the finished part. #3472 had to refuse every part-off there, which refuses a legal program (issue comments of 2026-11-22).

## Readings (3 mm GT-0300 blade, orientation 2: the -Z corner is posted)

| case | kerf | posted Z |
|---|---|---|
| #3452 pin, end face Z-70, default | Z-73..-70 | Z-73 (no change) |
| same, back stock 0.5 | Z-73.5..-70.5 | Z-73.5 |
| same, chuck piece | refused: "nothing to part ... stands wholly on the free-end side (higher Z) ... set 'The part is' to 'Cut-off piece'" | - |
| stubbed pin in the OP20 flip setup, plane Z-14, default | refused by name (names 'Chuck piece') | - |
| same, chuck piece | Z-14..-11 | Z-14 (the part's end face) |
| motion: part Z0..70 in the chuck, stub to Z84, plane Z70, chuck piece | Z70..73 | - |
| same, chuck piece, back stock 1 | Z71..74 | - |

## Tests

New pins. Each was red on the unchanged code (#3472 head 6c18258d1): the motion and app pins did not compile (no `PartKerf`, no `kerf` field), and the flip pin is refused there.

- `crates/motion/tests/turning_part_kept.rs` (new, 5 tests):
  - `the_default_setting_parts_the_3452_case_as_before`
  - `a_back_stock_moves_the_whole_kerf_into_the_bar`: the kerf, and the refusal of the default kerf "0.500 mm into the 0.500 mm back stock".
  - `the_chuck_piece_turns_the_kerf_to_the_free_end`: the kerf, no rule note, and the refusal of the default kerf on that model ("3.000 mm past", "free-end side (higher Z)").
  - `the_chuck_piece_with_no_model_below_the_plane_is_refused_by_name`
  - `a_back_stock_that_is_not_a_size_is_refused`: -0.1, NaN, infinity, in the kernel and in the verdict.
- `crates/app/tests/lathe_part_off_kerf.rs` (4 new tests):
  - `a_flipped_setup_keeping_the_chuck_piece_cuts_the_stub_off_the_free_end`: generates, posts Z-14.
  - `a_back_stock_posts_the_kerf_that_far_into_the_bar`: posts Z-73.5.
  - `the_chuck_piece_with_nothing_in_the_chuck_is_refused_by_name`
  - `the_kerf_setting_is_an_undoable_edit_and_rides_the_project_file`: no key at the default, a negative back stock refused by `EditOperationParams::new`, edit, undo, redo, save and open.
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_part_kerf.rs` (new): `edit_operation_sets_the_kept_piece_and_back_stock_and_undo_restores_them`.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/part_kerf_tests.rs` (new): `the_kept_piece_row_names_both_pieces_and_its_pick_applies_and_undoes`.

Changed pin (expected): `a_flipped_setup_refuses_the_part_off_by_name` now asks for the new refusal text ("cannot keep the cut-off piece", "'Chuck piece'").

Mechanical: each `OpParams::Part` and `PartParams` literal in the tests gets `kerf: Default::default()`.

### Mutation checks (each guard put back to the old code, then restored)

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| kernel uses `chuck_side()` and the plane (ignores the setting) | RED: 3 tests of `turning_part_kept` |
| verdict ignores the back stock zone | RED: `a_back_stock_moves_the_whole_kerf_into_the_bar` |
| verdict uses `chuck_side()` (ignores `kept`) | RED: 2 chuck-piece tests |
| flip refusal unconditional again (the #3472 code) | RED: `a_flipped_setup_keeping_the_chuck_piece_cuts_the_stub_off_the_free_end` |
| no back stock check at the command door | RED: `the_kerf_setting_is_an_undoable_edit_and_rides_the_project_file` |

After the restore, all pins are green.

### Gate

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main --dry-run` plans 730 steps (the motion change reaches every app binary). Thus each touched binary ran alone, debug, on head c6230e2a0:

- motion: `--lib` 536 passed (10 ignored); `turning_part_kept` 5; `turning_part_kerf` 6; `turning_blade` 11; `turning_stock` 5; `turning_contour_stock` 4.
- app: `lathe_part_off_kerf` 8; `mcp_part_kerf` 1; `lathe_blade_corner` 4; `catalog_groove_part_off` 1; `lathe_post` 7; `lathe_post_inch` 6; `turning_blade` 14; `setup_align_lathe` 4; `turning_stock_approach` 3; `drill_prior` 12; `coarse_laws` 6; `project_roundtrip` 76; `mcp_enum_patch` 3; `--lib part` 17.
- app `example_catalog -- groove cone`: 5 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `turning_cone_thread_case_posts_the_taper_and_the_thread` (`example_catalog.rs:311`, "the part-off reaches the axis"). It is in #3472, not in this PR. #3472 changed `cone-thread.nc` to `G01 X0. Z12.`, but the test still asks for `Z13.5`. This PR does not touch either file, and the two `regenerates` tests pass (the default posts the same bytes).
- ui: `--lib` 1432 passed (7 ignored).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Heavy lanes

GREEN on `c6230e2a0c5c6f9a7631c5a3386cc06e326310e1`: **244 steps, 0 failed**, 86.2 minutes. The gate ran all motion and app heavy targets, including the release build. The tool accepted the known-fail entries for #1950 and #2849 as red as expected.

Command: `RUSTC_WRAPPER= CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1 cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`.

At the start, `upstream/main` was `ebc5cadd46bd171465b93acb3e52e6d4488c498a`. During the run, the local ref advanced to `69997a6ded2d6ca559601c9233629045caabecda`. Explicit-base dry runs select the same 244 steps and exact Cargo commands for both SHAs.

### Full catalog comparison

title: fix(drilling): a mill names radial holes in skipped, never in cross
body:
## What changed

- On a machine of kind `Mill`, Detect holes does not store radial holes in the Drill op's `cross` list.
- Each radial hole goes into `skipped`, with its size, origin and direction.
- The Z holes stay in `holes`, and the op generates.
- If no Z hole remains, Detect holes refuses. The refusal names each radial hole.
- A lathe or a mill-turn keeps the old behaviour. The `cross` list is filled there.
- The rule is in the new module `crates/app/src/operation/cross_reach.rs`. The test is the same `Kind::Mill` test that Generate uses for its "no turret" refusal.

## Cause

- #2601 made Detect holes store radial holes on every machine. Generate then refused them on a mill.
- On a mill with Z holes and a radial hole, Generate refused with "Z holes AND cross holes".
- `edit_operation` cannot clear `cross`, because the field is not in the params patch. The user could only delete the op.

## Tests

- New pin `drilling_detect_mill_radial::a_mill_skips_radial_holes_by_name_and_the_z_holes_generate`. The fixture is a plate with two D6 Z holes beside a bar with one blind D6 radial hole, on a mill, through MCP. The test expects `holes: 2`, `radial_holes: 0`, one `skipped` sentence, and a generate status of `ok`.
- New pin `drilling_detect_mill_radial::a_mill_with_only_radial_holes_refuses_detection_by_name`.
- Red before the fix: yes, both. Upstream answered `{"holes":2,"radial_holes":1,"skipped":[]}` (the issue's symptom).
- Changed test `drilling_detect_opposite::mill_detection_names_opposite_blind_radial_holes_and_stores_none`. The #2601 test pinned the old behaviour. It now checks the two opposite blind holes through `cross_holes_of` (the #2601 recognizer coverage stays), and it checks the new mill refusal.
- Mutation: with the old `material.rs` back, both new pins fail. With the fix restored, they pass.
- Gate: the quick gate selects all 317 app suites for a lib change. That is far over the 5-minute budget. I ran the narrow ladder instead: the app lib tests and 30 suites that call `detect_holes` or do cross drilling (`mcp`, `drill_undersize`, `drilling_cross*`, `lathe_cross_drill`, `setup_align_*`, `bore_*`, `thread_*` and others). All are green. `camcraft-ui` lib `detect` tests: 7 green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- The issue's real STEP part on the Tormach 770MX + microARC 4 after `lay_part_on_face`. The pin uses a synthetic part on the default mill.
- The full quick gate over all 317 app suites.
- `cross` stays outside `edit_operation`. The issue accepts either fix. On a mill no `cross` list is filled now.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes `material.rs` or the two test files. `material.rs` was 421 lines before this PR and is now 426. A split is a separate task.

Changelog: Detect holes on a mill names each radial hole in `skipped` and keeps the Z holes, so the Drill op generates instead of refusing "Z holes AND cross holes".

title: fix(post): refuse an upright section after a tilt when the script does not declare uprightReturn
body:
Stacked on #3478 (merge #3478 first). This PR merges the #3478 head (`48c17f6c3`) and adds its own commits on top.

## What changed
- New manifest flag `uprightReturn = true`. It says: the script retracts to a safe height and commands the rotaries to zero at the start of each section that follows a tilted section.
- New engine pass `crates/post/src/post/upright_after_tilt.rs`. `engine::run_program_with` calls it before the hooks.
  - It tracks the modal A/B/C from the last move that states them.
  - It finds the first section whose first motion record states no A/B/C, after a section that left a rotary off zero. A motion record is a `MOVE` or a `CYCLE`. A canned cycle states no rotary angle (review of 5796026b4).
  - If the script does not declare the flag, the engine adds one counted warning. The warning names the two operations and the flag. A warning blocks the post in the app.
  - A C angle of C-axis live-tool work (`PARAM LiveTool`) does not count as a tilt. That law is section-scoped (#33).
- `fanuc.cps`, `doosan-dnm.cps`, `mach4.cps` and `tormach.cps` declare the flag.
- The Mach4 AC trunnion fixture moved from `mach4_trunnion.rs` to the shared module `crates/post/tests/ac_trunnion_support/mod.rs`. No test of `mach4_trunnion.rs` changed.
- `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` lists and explains the flag.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/3477-upright-after-tilt-flag.md`.

## Cause
- `post::dump` writes no angle on a move without a leaning axis. The angle words are modal.
- Only the script can command the return. #3478 makes the Fanuc and Doosan posts do it. Tormach and Mach4 already did it.
- No law made a script of the user (`PostRef::File`) do it. Such a script posted an upright operation after a tilted operation at the old lean, and no check stopped it.

## Name of the flag
The issue gives `uprightAfterTilt` as an example name. #3478 already defines a script function `uprightAfterTilt()` in `fanuc.cps` and `doosan-dnm.cps`. A top-level `uprightAfterTilt = true` replaces that function, and the post fails with `TypeError: not a callable function`. Thus the flag is `uprightReturn`.

## Tests
New pins in `camcraft-post` `upright_after_tilt`:
- `a_script_without_upright_after_tilt_is_refused_by_name`: a copy of fanuc and doosan-dnm without the flag, tilted then upright, tool 1 and tool 2. Red before the fix: yes (`fanuc (tool 1): the engine refuses the upright section by name: []`).
- `each_shipped_rotary_post_declares_upright_after_tilt`: fanuc, doosan-dnm, mach4, tormach. Red before the fix: yes.
- `a_script_without_upright_after_tilt_posts_a_program_with_no_return_to_state`: no refusal for tilted only, tilted then tilted, upright then tilted, upright then upright.
- `mach4_states_upright_after_an_indexed_section` (issue item 4): retract, then `A0`, then the first X/Y traverse. It passes on unchanged code. Mach4 already did the return; this pins it.

- `a_cycle_that_opens_an_upright_section_after_a_tilt_is_refused_by_name` (review finding 1): fanuc without the flag, a tilted section, then a cycle-only section, and a cycle before a later move that states zero angles. Red before the fix: yes (`cycle only: the engine refuses the cycle section by name: ["tilted move inside a canned-cycle group", ...]`, no `uprightReturn` warning).

Unit tests in `post::upright_after_tilt::tests`: the refusal text, a table C left off zero, a stated zero, a live-tool C, a re-stated tilt, a cycle-only section (`a_cycle_only_section_after_a_lean_is_refused_by_name`), and a cycle before a stated zero (`a_cycle_before_a_later_stated_zero_is_refused`).

Mutations:
- `engine.rs` from base (no call): `a_script_without_upright_after_tilt_is_refused_by_name` is red. Restored: green.
- `fanuc.cps` from base (no flag): `each_shipped_rotary_post_declares_upright_after_tilt` and the two Fanuc posting pins are red (refused by the new law). Restored: green.
- `upright_after_tilt.rs` without the `Record::Cycle` arm: the integration pin and the two cycle unit tests are red. Restored: green.

Gates on the final head `d563eecb2`, against `upstream/main` (`0d7263ac4`):
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 226 steps, 0 failed. This includes `app suites: example_catalog`, `app suites: conformance` and `post suites: upright_after_tilt`.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: 205 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Both gates ran with `CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1`. The target seed from another worktree gave a stale build (`can't find crate`), not a code failure.

## Goldens moved
- `examples/catalog/multiaxis/indexed/indexed.nc`: this change comes from #3478 (commit `48c17f6c3`, merged into this branch). The `uprightAfterTilt()` return of #3478 adds `G91 G28 Z0` / `G90` / `G00 A0.` after `G90 G54 G40 G49 G80` in the sections "Back pocket" and "Tilted pocket". This PR itself moves no golden: the flag is a manifest line, and the cycle check adds no output line. `catalog_multiaxis_indexed::regenerates` and `::rebuilds` pass.

## Not exercised
- The app post gate in a GUI session with a user post. The engine warning is the path that `posting.rs` already blocks on.
- A real control.
- A stream from an outside `.cnc` producer whose tilted section states its angle only after its first move. The law refuses such a section after a tilt when the flag is absent. That is the safe side.

## Overlaps
- #3478: this PR is stacked on it (`fanuc.cps`, `doosan-dnm.cps`, `upright_after_tilt.rs`).
- #3471 touches `fanuc.cps`, `doosan-dnm.cps`, `mach4.cps`, `tormach.cps` and `post/mod.rs`. Different functions and lines (this PR adds one manifest line in each post and one `mod` line). Whichever merges second refreshes.
- #3483 touches `tormach.cps` (manifest line 26 and other functions). Different lines. Whichever merges second refreshes.
- #3046 touches `engine.rs`, `post/mod.rs` and `assets/posts/AGENTS.md`. Different lines. Whichever merges second refreshes.
- #3468, #3441 touch `fanuc.cps` in other functions. #3312 touches `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` in another section.

Changelog: A post script that does not declare `uprightReturn = true` is now refused by name when an operation with no stated rotary angles follows a tilted operation, so a user's own post can no longer cut an upright operation with the axes still tilted.

Effort: high

Fixes #3477

title: fix(post): post a short arc whose written ends share one angle as a straight move
body:
Stacked on #3471 (merge #3471 first).

## What changed
- `arcFateOf` (`crates/post/src/post/arc_guard.rs`) has one more rule. The written start and the written end differ, but they are on one ray from the written centre (the same angle). Or one end is on the written centre. If the record turns half a circle or less, the answer is `"linear"`. The post writes its straight feed move.
- The rule reads the numbers of the written words. It uses only the zero of the cross product and the sign of the dot product. A mirrored axis or a lathe diameter word does not change these.
- A record whose own ends in the stream are on one ray (stream sweep 0) stays an arc. `emitArcWithRadius` reads that as a full turn.
- `fanuc-lathe.cps` and `tormach-lathe.cps` now write the feed move for `"linear"` in their meridian arc path. Before, they wrote no block for any answer that was not `"arc"`.
- The old inline sweep code moved into the helper `_arcSweep`. Its behaviour did not change.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/3474-same-angle-arc.md`.

## Cause
The #3442 guard compares only the written ends. When the ends differ only along the radius, the guard returned `"arc"`. On the parent branch every mill post wrote such a block. Examples:
- Fanuc mm: `G01 X10.011 Y5.` then `G03 X10.01 Y5. Z5.5 I-0.011 J0. F180`.
- LinuxCNC inch: `G1 X0.4011 Y0.2` then `G3 X0.401 Y0.2 Z0.2165 I-0.0011 J0 F7.09`.

The start and the end are at the same angle about the centre. The radii are 0.011 and 0.010. RS-274 / ISO 6983 reads an arc whose end is at its start angle as a full turn. No control ran these blocks. A straight move is correct for each reading.

## Tests
New file `crates/post/tests/same_angle_arcs.rs`:
- `fanuc_and_linuxcnc_post_a_same_angle_arc_as_a_straight_move`: Fanuc and LinuxCNC, mm and inch. No arc block, and a straight move to the written end.
- `every_post_writes_a_same_angle_arc_as_its_straight_move`: all 14 mill posts in each unit that they offer, and the two lathes. The output is byte-equal to the straight feed to the same end. TinyG writes 4 decimals in mm. There the mm witness is a visible arc, and the test asserts that it stays one arc.
- `arc_fate_reads_a_same_angle_short_arc_as_a_straight_move`: the rule. Same angle, end on centre, a long CW record, an opposite end, a normal arc, and a stream sweep of zero.

All three were red on the parent head (#3471, `40e1baae7`).

Mutations (each put back, then restored):
- The guard of the parent PR: all 3 pins red.
- The `fanuc-lathe.cps` call site of the parent PR: `every_post_...` red (`fanuc-lathe mm`).
- The `tormach-lathe.cps` call site of the parent PR: `every_post_...` red (`tormach-lathe mm`).
- No `sweep > 1e-9` term: `radius_arcs::near_180_and_full_circle_arcs_in_all_planes_hold_chord_and_center` and `arc_fate_...` red.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base base-3471` (the parent head): 75 steps, 0 failed. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved
None.

## Not exercised
- No control ran the blocks. The reading of the controls is from RS-274 / ISO 6983, not from a run.
- A written end behind the written start (a written sweep of nearly a full turn on a short record). We found no input that makes it. It is recorded as dropped in the decision.
- The rule uses the written absolute centre word. The control's centre is the start plus the written `I J`. The two can differ by one output step.
- Mill-turn, plasma and wire posts get the rule through the same `arcFate` call. They have no witness in the new file.

## Overlaps
- Stacked on #3471: it adds `arc_guard.rs` and `arcFateOf`, which this PR changes. Retarget this PR to `main` before #3471 merges.

Changelog: A post now writes a straight move for a very small arc whose written start and end have the same angle about the centre. Before, a control could read the block as a full turn.

Fixes #3474

title: fix(multiaxis): rotate the rotaries before the first five-axis approach descent
body:
## What changed

Five-axis generators set the first station's pose on the modal builder
and then pushed the descend to first contact, so the rotary swing rode
the approach move: the machine turned the A/C head while the tool
descended, and the ball swept through unknown air and through the rim
it approached.

The fix splits the approach. The pose is stated as its own zero-travel
Rapid (a standstill rotary index - the tip held on the hop plane, or at
the tip the machine already holds), and the Plunge/cut descends under
the pose already stated:

- `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/curve.rs` (`contour_curve`): every
  chain's approach swings first, then plunges.
- `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/stamp.rs` (the stamp emit loop, all
  posed kinds - parallel5d, flow5d, swarf5d, rough, contour5d): at
  every rapid-to-cut re-entry where the pose changes, the swing is
  emitted at a standstill before the cut. Intermediate cut moves keep
  the modal tilt law unchanged.

No new `MoveKind`. The builder already keeps a zero-travel move whose
pose changed (it drops one only when the tip AND the pose both stand),
and the post already solves a zero-travel segment as a pure rotary
reorientation (`ds_tip == 0` in `crates/post/src/post/g93.rs`), so the
swing always commands. That is the answer to the zero-travel question:
the swing is a zero-travel rapid, not a short travel move - a travel
move would drag the tip sideways while the head turns, and a dropped
zero-travel move cannot occur, because a drop needs the pose to match
the held one, in which case no rotation is due.

## Readings

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 28 steps, 0 failed
  (motion lib 536 passed, multiaxis, multiaxis_avoid, multiaxis_rough,
  pivot5d, swarf_pose_continuity, app operations, posed_contact and the
  rest all green).
- The existing laws were amended where the swing touches them, each in
  its own terms: a TRAVEL rapid still inherits its pose
  (`rapids_hold_the_pose_they_inherit`, `rapid_pose_contract` - the
  zero-travel index is the second legal way a rapid states a pose,
  beside the swarf link's ball-centred swing); the air-link ratchet
  counts travel links only; the pivot-law ball readers skip the
  swing (it cuts nothing) through `no_swings`/`sans_swings` helpers.
- A decision record sits in `docs/decisions/3414-approach-rotary-order.md`.

## Pinning tests

- `the_approach_rotates_before_it_descends` (crates/motion/tests/pivot5d.rs):
  a zero-travel rotary swing precedes the first descend; the plunge
  holds the pose the swing stated; no pose change rides any move that
  crosses from air to material, over contour_curve, parallel5d, flow5d
  and swarf5d.

## What was not exercised

- No posted G-code golden was regenerated (the post's pure-rotary path
  is covered by its own suite; the swing was not posted end to end on
  a real machine file).
- The heavy lanes were not run; the diff touches `camcraft-motion`, so
  the release-tier lane check stays with the review/cut.

## Changelog

Five-axis approach moves rotate the machine to the first pose before
the tool descends to the part, no longer while it descends.

Fork synced at v0.25.0.

Fixes #3414

title: fix(multiaxis): close the Rotary Offset Zigzag levels with a ring that skips the seam
body:
## What changed

Rotary Offset Zigzag levels now finish their walls with a ring, as the
planar #3129 levels already do. On the wrap the plan drops only the
seam's own edges: a boundary loop that spans a whole period wraps the
seam, and its two cover-end edges are the seam's two copies at one
azimuth. That loop's ring keeps one period of boundary per leftover arc;
each arc arrives open and ends on the seam copy of its start azimuth -
closed on the work - while the rows cut the seam columns. A loop that
wraps no azimuth closes exactly as the planar ring always did. The
no-seam path is byte-for-byte the old `zigzag_ringed_passes` behaviour.

Before the fix the wrap kept its rows alone, so every wall perpendicular
to the rows kept cusps between row ends. Measured on the new test's
D-flat: the worst wall scallop falls from 0.071 mm to under 0.02 mm at
every level between the flat and the skin.

Placement: `machining2d::pocket_zigzag::ringed_passes` (the seam law,
one `Option<f64>` period), called from `machining3d::hsm::plan_level`.
Decision record: `docs/decisions/3168-rotary-zigzag-seam-rings.md`.

## Pinning tests

New suite `crates/motion/tests/rotary_zigzag_rings.rs`:

- `the_wrapped_ring_cuts_no_azimuth_twice` - on a developed cover two
  periods wide, the target band's ring cuts every azimuth once: no
  azimuth bin takes radial feed runs in both directions, and the band's
  walls stay within the wall-reach bound. This is the failure the old
  "a ring there would cut one seam line twice" comment feared.
- `the_dflat_edge_walls_are_ringed` - a D-flat bar wraps and its edge
  walls (perpendicular to the rows) finish within the wall-reach bound
  at every level between the flat and the skin. Run against the unfixed
  tree it fails with `scallop 0.071 mm`.

## What was not exercised

- The Adaptive seam law (`Seam::crossed_by`, the named refusals) is

title: fix(2d): Pass starts at (Auto/Inside/Outside) for Bore
body:
Stacked on #3353 (merge #3353 first).

## What changed

Bore takes the shared "Pass starts at" parameter of #3316. No new type.

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/bore.rs`: new entry `bore_started(p, pass_start)`. It orders the rings of each level with `PassStart::rank`. The old `bore(p)` calls it with Auto.
  - Ring `k` (1 is the innermost ring, `count` is the wall ring) is the offset index `count - k` from the wall, in the outer family. A hole disk has no hole family.
  - Auto: the centre-out walk. This is the old loop order, so Auto output does not change.
  - Outside: the wall ring first, then each ring in to the centre.
  - Inside: the rank law gives the centre-out order, because a hole has no inner wall. Inside is the same path as Auto.
  - Each level still dives at the centre. The entry law (plunge, ramp along the radial sweep, the centre-cutting law) does not change.
- `OpParams::Bore.pass_start`: the seed is Auto. `EditOperationParams` carries it with undo. The digest writes it only off Auto (the #3316 bytes).
- Project key `pass_start` on the Bore DTO. `auto` is never written. No version step.
- MCP: the generic `edit_operation` door. The #3316 patch guard finds the field by itself.
- UI: the shared `Pass starts at` row on the Bore Passes tab, with a Bore hint (Inside is the centre-out order).
- User guide: the Bore table row and one paragraph.
- Decision file `docs/decisions/3360-bore-pass-start.md`. It leaves room for the #1448 start point and exit point.
- Test fixtures: 13 `OpParams::Bore` literals get `pass_start: Auto`.

## Cause

Bore had a fixed ring order (centre out). The maintainer asked that every kind with an order of passes or rings gets the shared option (#3316).

## Hand trace, one level

Ø20 hole, Ø6 cutter, rc = 7, 3 rings (rho 2.33, 4.67, 7.0), kmax = 2:
- Auto: ranks 0, 1, 2 for k = 1, 2, 3. Order 2.33, 4.67, 7.0 (as before).
- Outside: ranks 2, 1, 0. Order 7.0, 4.67, 2.33. The sweep goes from the centre to the wall ring start, then each chord goes in by one ring.
- Inside: ranks 3, 4, 5. Order 2.33, 4.67, 7.0.

## Tests

Pins:
- `camcraft-motion` `bore_pass_start`:
  - `bore_outside_starts_each_level_on_the_wall_and_walks_in`. Red on the stub that ignored the value: `Outside cuts the wall ring first: [2.33, 4.67, 7.0]`.
  - `bore_auto_keeps_the_centre_out_ladder_byte_for_byte` (`bore` equals `bore_started(Auto)`, move for move).
  - `bore_inside_is_the_centre_out_order`.
- `camcraft-app` `bore_pass_start`:
  - `bore_outside_cuts_the_wall_ring_first_through_generate`.
  - `bore_pass_start_is_undoable_and_rides_the_project_file`.
  - `mcp_sets_bore_pass_start_refuses_an_unknown_word_and_undo_restores_it`.
- `camcraft-ui` lib `egui_app::tests::pass_start::the_bore_passes_tab_offers_pass_start_and_shows_the_draft`, and the Bore row in `every_field_lives_on_exactly_one_section`.

Mutations:
- The ring sort disabled in `bore.rs`: the motion pin goes red. Restored: green.
- The Bore arm of generate passes Auto instead of the op value: the app pin goes red. Restored: green.

Runs on the final head (debug, without sccache):
- motion: lib 533 ok; `bore_pass_start` 3; `bore_ramp_angle` 2; `bore_carried_ramp` 2; `machining2d` 68; `center_cut_law` 7; `level_links` 13; `top_z_level` 12; `refusal_ghost` 5; `equal_steps` 13; `entry_ramp_angle` 3. All ok.
- app: lib 297 ok; `bore_pass_start` 3; `bore_entry` 4; `bore_core` 6; `break_through` 12; `coarse_rims` 5; `conformance` 7; `golden_cl` 33; `hole_wall_flats` 5; `ladder_entry_height` 5; `lathe_workholding_kinds` 10 (1 ignored); `mcp_enum_patch` 3; `mill2d_c` 9; `offset_pass_start` 3; `project_roundtrip` 76; `refusal_location` 3; `setup_align_hole_kinds` 4; `stepped_stock_rapid` 8; `stock_source_holes` 9; `stock_source_verdict` 22; `thread_mill_rim` 13. All ok.
- ui: lib 1425 ok.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Gate

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` did not complete. The diff against `upstream/main` includes all of #3353, so the plan had several hundred app binaries. All 82 motion steps passed. Then the app build step did not finish within the 2-hour background limit: the shared sccache server stalled while other workers built. The runs above replace it, without sccache. The full quick gate is **not run** on this head.

## Goldens moved

None. `golden_cl` (33) and `conformance` (7) pass with no golden change.

## Not exercised

- Heavy lanes: not run.
- Outside with a through hole, with stock to leave and with several holes is not pinned. The ring order code is the same for each hole.
- Outside makes the wall ring a full slot in solid stock, and the wall is cut before the inner rings. This is what the option asks for. Auto stays the default.
- No GUI screenshot.
- The `camcraft-mcp` skill row for Bore is not added: the edit of `.claude/skills/` needed an approval in this session. The #3316 row already names the key.

## Overlaps

- #3353: the parent. This PR adds Bore beside 2D Offset in the same files (`pass_start_row.rs`, `params.rs`, `params_impl.rs`, `generate.rs`, `mill2d` digest). Merge #3353 first.
- #3387 (Face, also stacked on #3353) touches `pass_start_row.rs`, `generate.rs`, `params.rs`: different functions. Whichever merges second refreshes.
- #3103 (Bore Helical strategy, `needs-rework`) touches `bore.rs` (`BoreParams`, `validate`) and the Bore params: different functions. Whichever merges second refreshes.

title: feat(tools): one tool meridian for each mill kind, split into convex atoms
body:
## What changed

- A new module `camcraft_tools::meridian` adds the tool meridian. The meridian is the cutting outline `rho(z)` of a mill, tip up. It is made of lines and circular arcs.
- `Meridian` uses the `SpunPoint` form (`z`, `r`, signed `arc`). It holds one cutting flag for each segment. A pilot bearing band is a non-cutting segment.
- `Tool::meridian()` gives the meridian of these kinds: `EndMill`, `BallNose`, `BullNose`, `Drill`, `Taper`, `TSlot`, `Keyseat`, `Dovetail`, `Lollipop`.
- `Meridian::atoms(bound, sag)` splits the meridian into convex solids of revolution:
  - a line gives a frustum;
  - an arc that bulges away from the axis gives a torus zone;
  - an arc that bulges toward the axis gives chord frusta (`Bound::Outer`) or tangent frusta (`Bound::Inner`). Each part stays within the sag limit.
- Each atom carries the cutting flag of its segment.
- Degenerate input gives a named `MeridianError`. It never panics.
- No consumer reads the meridian yet. No toolpath, simulation, check or posted output changes.

## Cause

This is sub-issue 1 of #3351 (option C, the hybrid shape model). The maintainer asked for tapered and router tooling. Later sub-issues make the consumers read the tool shape through this meridian.

## Tests

Pins:

- `verify::probe_meridian_tests::meridian_atoms_match_cutter_atoms_for_each_mill_kind` (camcraft-sim lib). For 12 tools of each listed kind, the meridian atoms are the solids that `Cutter::atoms` builds today. The test compares `z0`, `z1` and `rho` at 65 heights, within 1e-9 mm. The cases include a ball and a bull nose shorter than the corner, and a cone taller than the flute.
- `meridian::tests::meridian_agrees_with_profile_on_the_cutting_band` (camcraft-tools lib). The meridian agrees with `Tool::profile` at each profile vertex on the cutting band.
- `meridian::tests::concave_arc_outer_bound_contains_and_inner_bound_stays_inside`. For sag limits 0.1, 0.01 and 0.001 mm: the outer union contains the arc, the inner union stays inside it, and each sag is under the limit. The bearing band is the one non-cutting atom.
- `meridian::tests::degenerate_meridians_are_refused_by_name`: too few points, zero-length segment, negative radius, non-finite value, arc tighter than its chord, segment that runs back, arc that folds, concave arc through the axis, flag count, bad sag limit, sag limit too fine.
- `meridian::tests::tool_meridian_refuses_bad_tools_by_name`: a kind that is not a mill, NaN, negative and zero diameter, a bull corner over half the diameter, a dovetail that `undercut::refusal` names.

Red before the change: the sim pin did not compile (`E0432: unresolved import camcraft_tools::meridian`, `E0599: no method named meridian`).

The first green run found float dust: `bull: rho(0) 3.0000000298023224 vs 3`. A centre error of 1e-16 gives 3e-8 mm of error at the z extreme of the circle. The fix snaps the centre when an arc end sits at the centre's radius.

Mutation checks (each red, then restored and green):

- fold guard removed: `degenerate_meridians_are_refused_by_name` red (`Ok(..)` vs `Err(ArcFolds(1))`).
- through-axis guard removed: the same test red (`Ok(..)` vs `Err(Negative(1))`).
- outer and inner bounds swapped: `concave_arc_outer_bound_contains_and_inner_bound_stays_inside` red (`outer under the arc at z 4.01`).
- centre snap absent: the sim pin red (`bull: rho(0) 3.0000000298023224 vs 3`).

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 122 steps, 0 failed. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. After the clippy fix (two equivalent comparisons), the tools and sim lib suites ran again: 115 and 233 passed.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- No consumer reads the meridian, so no end-to-end path runs through it.
- No real router bit record (roundover, cove) exists yet. The concave-arc tests use a hand-built roundover meridian.
- Heavy lanes: not run. The change adds no code on any generator or law path.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes these files.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/3367-tool-meridian.md`.

Effort: max

Changelog: Tools: a tool meridian (lines and arcs) for each mill kind, split into convex atoms with outer and inner bounds for concave arcs (internal; no output change).

Fixes #3367

title: fix(2d): keep exterior contours at their requested depths
body:
## What changed

Exterior contour rings that the user picks keep every requested depth when the complete cutter-center ring clears the model's XY convex hull.
The sign plate reaches Z 0 and keeps its four tabs.
Picked contours refuse generation when a required deeper section cannot be read.
The error names the section failure and the skipped levels.

The hull proof applies only to picked rings (`contour_on_picked`, through `ladder_picked`).
The whole-model contour and the unpicked region contour keep the plain `ladder`.
A whole-model contour on a broken mesh must refuse when a section cannot be read.
The hull proof skips each section, so it must not hide that refusal.

## Cause

The depth ladder read interior sections even for a cutter outside the complete model footprint.
A failed section could become a false floor.
The picked-ring check accepted this partial path after an earlier level succeeded.

## Tests

Final head: 813e6a8cc. Base: `upstream/main` at 6e641dac7.

Pins:

- `outside_sign_plate_reaches_bottom_with_four_tabs` (motion `contour_outside_floor`) checks every requested depth and four bottom cut runs.

- `whole_model_contour_that_cannot_reach_bottom_is_refused_with_the_stopped_level` (app `contour_whole_step`, unchanged) checks that a whole-model contour on a broken mesh refuses.

Pin proof:

- The first two pins fail when the original `upstream/main` depth code is restored. The plate pin reports floor Z 7.061. The unread-section pin returns a partial path.
- The third pin fails when the hull proof is put back into the shared `ladder`. It reports `deepest=-0.5`, the same failure that the review found. It passes when the fix is restored.

- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test contour_outside_floor`: 2 passed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test example_catalog`: 37 passed, 4 ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Gate map gap: the quick gate does not select app `contour_whole_step` for this diff. The suite imports only `camcraft_app` re-exports, so the map does not link it to `motion::machining2d`.

The mesh fixture contains only the `sign` entity's saved triangles from the [reported q04 project](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q04-vcarve-sign/q04-vcarve-sign-posted-5ops.camproj).

- `CreateSetup` writes the next order: one past the highest stored order, 0 for the first setup.
- `CreateSetup` refuses creation when the highest stored order is `u32::MAX`. The refusal preserves the document and program order.
- `setup::setups` sorts by `order`. Setups without an order (older files) sort first, by name. This is the old behaviour for these files.
- The project file saves `order` on the setup row. `PROJECT_VERSION` steps from 76 to 77 (second review). A v76 file has no `order`; it opens unchanged and keeps name order. A v76 reader refuses a v77 file.
- `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.camproj` states version 77. `deburr_chord_width.rs` now pins `>= 76` and the current version, not the literal 76.
- `add_setup`, `get_job`, `operation_order` and the post all read `setup::setups`. They now all follow the creation order.
- Comments in `setup.rs` that said "by name" now say "program order".

## Cause

`setup::setups` returned the setups in name order. `Front_A90` sorted before `Setup1`. Thus it was listed and posted first, although it took its datum and stock from `Setup1`.

## Tests

- New pin `crates/app/tests/setup_creation_order.rs`:
  - `a_setup_created_second_stays_second_whatever_its_name`: `Setup1`, then `Front_A90` (datum from `Setup1`). The names and the operation order keep the creation order. A third setup goes last. Delete and undo give it back its place.
  - `the_creation_order_survives_save_and_load_and_reaches_the_post`: save, `open_project` over MCP, `get_job` and `add_setup` list the creation order, and the posted program has `Setup1`'s operation before `Front_A90`'s.
- Red before the fix: both tests failed (`left: ["Front_A90", "Setup1"]`).
- Mutations:
  - Remove the sort in `setup::setups`: both pins red.
  - Save writes `order: None` (`wire.rs`): the save/load pin red.
  - Load reads `order: None` (`apply.rs`): the save/load pin red.
  - Each restored: green.
- Changed test `setup_delete_order.rs`: it pinned the old name-order law (its fixture created `B_Middle` last and expected it in the middle by name). The fixture now creates A, B, C in that order. The test still pins that undo of `DeleteSetup` restores the middle place and the posted program.
- Final head: `e0e87fa1218e5d5964f6657e1d6dca46751c30e1`.
- Base: `upstream/main` `ef157211438104997fc9e51f7e3affc4db303545`, fetched after upstream advanced during the first gate run.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 60 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: 207 steps, 0 failed, 41.5 minutes. The release build and all app heavy targets passed. The gate handled #1950 and #2849 as expected failures.
- Heavy lanes: `app heavy: lib`, `bins`, every selected integration target, and `doc`. The setup command change selects every app heavy target.
- First heavy run against base `148a5c832aa811bab9cae5c7f69e0ad945ee92d4`: 207 steps, 0 failed. Both gates were repeated after the base advanced.
- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed on the final head.
- `cargo test -j 6 -p camcraft-app --test conformance --test golden_cl --test solid_law_goldens`: passed. Counts: 7, 33 and 7.
- The quick gate ran `app suites: example_catalog`: 37 passed, 4 ignored. It also ran `example_catalog_adaptive`: 1 passed.
- New pin: `exhausted_setup_order_refuses_creation_without_changing_the_program`. It uses the final available order and loads that project. Creation then refuses without changing the document, setup order or operation order.
- Pin proof: restore both production files from the reviewed head, then run the new pin. It fails with `exhausted order must refuse creation`. Restore the fix and run `setup_creation_order`: 3 passed.
- The commands used `RUSTC_WRAPPER=` and `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1`. Gates set `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`.

## Second review round (head `4df4fc9f7`)

- New pin: `a_v76_file_keeps_name_order_and_a_newer_file_is_refused`. A v76 file with no `order` opens with name order (setups and operations). It saves again with only the version changed. A file one version newer is refused.
- Pin proof: set `PROJECT_VERSION` back to 76. The pin fails (`setup order needs project v77`). Restore 77: `setup_creation_order` 4 passed, `setup_delete_order` 2 passed.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 62 steps. One step failed on the first run: `deburr_chord_width` pinned the literal 76. After the fix, `--failed` ran that step: passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `conformance`: 7 passed. `golden_cl`: 33 passed. `continuous_4axis_part` version test: passed. The quick gate ran `example_catalog` and `example_catalog_adaptive`: passed.
- Heavy lanes: not run for this round. The second review says heavy lanes are not a condition for this PR (maintainer decision of 2026-11-22, #3556). The reviewer runs the named suites on the trial merge.

## Goldens moved

Programs: none. Project: `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.camproj` changes only its version line (76 to 77), for the version step. The catalog, conformance, CL golden and solid-law golden suites ran. No `.nc`, `.cl` or `examples/catalog/**` file changed.

## Not exercised

- UI screenshots: no UI files changed. This fix adds a command refusal.
- The UI setup tree. It reads the same `setup::setups`; no UI test was added.
- A file saved by this build and opened by a released build. The version step makes a v76 build refuse it (`UnsupportedVersion`); the pin checks the refusal at `PROJECT_VERSION + 1`.

## Overlaps

- #3251 touches `crates/app/src/project/apply.rs` (`check_and_apply`), a different function. Whichever merges second refreshes.
- #2924 touches `crates/app/src/schema.rs` (`Sketch` doc comment), a different item. Whichever merges second refreshes.

## Follow-up

The reorder command and its MCP tool are filed as #3484.

Decision: `docs/decisions/3447-setup-creation-order.md`.

Effort: high

Changelog: Setups keep the order in which they were created; a setup added later is listed and posted after earlier setups, whatever its name.

Fixes #3447
