title: fix(2d): Pass starts at (Auto/Inside/Outside) for 2D Offset
body:
## What changed

A 2D Offset with an Outside containment cut each level core-first. On the band between the stock reach and the part, the core is the middle of the band, so the first ring was a full slot in the stock (#3316). This PR adds the shared parameter `PassStart { Auto, Inside, Outside }` and gives it to 2D Offset only.

### After the second read (comment 7077845657)

The second read found that the first ring law (`PassStart::rank`, an order of whole loops) still cut the full tool width where a ring splits at a narrow place: a split piece is one closed loop with stock-side arcs and part-side arcs. The red meter agreed: 7.97 mm on the second read's band, 8697 full-width points on fig8. The ring law is replaced:

- `crates/geometry/src/geo2d/clip_line.rs` (new): `Region::clip_polyline` and `Region::clip_ring`, an open-path clip against a region. Each segment splits at every boundary crossing, and a piece is kept by the parity of its midpoint. The direction is kept, every point lies on the input, and the wrap of a ring is joined. NaN and out-of-range input give a clean error. Tests: degenerate input (empty, one point, zero length, a path on the boundary, an empty region).
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/level_rings.rs` (new): Inside and Outside rings are level curves of the distance from the START side only. Outside: ring 0 is the stretch of the area's boundary on its outer edge; ring j is the outer edge (holes filled) eroded by j stepovers, clipped to the cutter-centre area as open pieces; the walls (the holes and the "Do not touch" keep-outs) come last, with the stock to leave. Inside is the mirror. Each piece is walked with the uncut side on the right for climb.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/level_order.rs` (new): each connected piece of the area is cut ring by ring, the nearest piece next. A piece joins the pass before it only by a chord that stays in the area, crosses no planned cut and runs through cut material (each sample within 0.9 tool radii of a walk already cut). Else the next pass starts on a vertex of a walk already cut, with a lead-in chord of the same law, so it re-enters a cleared column. The ends of the pieces are shared vertices of the boundary walks, so the crossing law reads touches.
- Keep-down pass links of this plan must also run through cleared columns (`ladder_links::through_cut`, `Motion::cleared_links`), else they lift by the existing rules (#3319 law).
- Visible warnings ("Pass start ..." notes; the op page shows each one as a `warning:` line, `approach_page::entry_status_lines`):
  - Outside, first ring on a wall: "Pass start Outside: the outer edge of this area is a wall in the stock, not the open stock edge, so each level starts with a cut of the full tool width along that wall".
  - Inside on an Outside band: "Pass start Inside: the inner edge of this area is the part wall, so each level starts with a cut of the full tool width along the part".
  - Inside round an island: "Pass start Inside: the inner edge of this area is an island wall, so each level starts with a cut of the full tool width along the island".
  - Each later cut at the full width: "Pass start <side>: N cut(s) take the full tool width where the area is narrower than the tool plus one stepover, or where a wall hides the start side; the first is at X .., Y ..".
  - The app passes the stock footprint in the area's frame (`operation/pass_start_stock.rs`), so a start ring in open air does not warn.
- `waterscan.rs` is main's file again; `PassStart::rank` is removed. Auto takes the old planner byte for byte (no golden changes).
- Texts corrected to what the tests prove: the `PassStart` docs, `docs/decisions/3316-pass-start-shared.md`, the hint in `pass_start_row.rs`, the `camcraft-mcp` skill row, the user guide (2D Offset, Pass starts at).
- New motion entry points `pocket_started_on` / `pocket_avoid_started_on` take a `StartSide` (start, stock footprint, around part); `pocket_started` / `pocket_avoid_started` keep a bare `PassStart`.

### After the third read (comment 7079896741, head 9939a6238)

The third read found a blocker: material nested in a hole stayed standing at full depth, with no warning. The Outside fill read the outer loops with `Region::new`, which turns a nested outer loop into a hole.

- `level_rings.rs`: each part of the material (an outer loop with the holes directly inside it) is planned from its own edges, at any depth of nesting (`material_parts`). Material inside a hole starts on its own edge (a wall in the stock: named by the wall-first warning). Inside on a part with no hole cuts that part from the middle outward, as Auto, with the note "Pass start Inside: N part(s) of this area have no hole to start from, so they are cut from the middle outward, as Auto cuts them". I did not take `Region::union_all` (the reader's proposal): it cuts the nested part with rings of the far outer edge, so its first cut lands in its middle at the full width.
- Completeness guard (`level_rings::unswept`): after the plan of a level, the passes are swept by the tool disc and compared with the cutter-centre area. If more than 0.1 mm2 stays unswept (read after a 50 um erosion), the plan is not posted. The level takes the Auto plan, and the toolpath says "Pass start <side>: the rings from the start side would leave A mm2 of this area uncut, so this area is cut in the Auto order instead". Recorded in the decision file.
- `clip_line.rs`: tests for a vertex exactly on the boundary, a tangent touch at a corner, and an overlap along a boundary edge in mid-segment.
- `pocket.rs` is 343 lines: `non_sliver_center` and its test moved to `pocket_plan.rs`. `levels.rs` did not grow in this fix (454 lines, 443 on main).
- Readings, shape-mask leftover (interior cells that the tool reaches and that stay uncut):
  - Ring-part fixture (stock 80 x 80, ring part 15..25): Outside on 9939a6238 153.7 mm2, 15103 interior cells; now 2.57 mm2, 0 interior cells. Inside now 2.63 mm2, 0 interior cells.
  - Hollow-boss pocket (80 x 60, boss radius 18, bore radius 10 cleared to the floor): Outside on 9939a6238 26.4 mm2, 1126 disallowed interior cells; now 15.1 mm2, all in the unreachable inside corners. Inside now 15.2 mm2, the same.
  - The "Do not touch" band: 10.8 mm2, all in the keep-out band of the pin (already true on 9939a6238; the check is new).

Unchanged from the first head: the type, the `OpParams` field, the project key `pass_start`, the MCP door, the Passes-tab row, the digest.


### After the delta review (head 3c3f13eb4; refresh merge of main 64b737729)

The delta review at `3c3f13eb4` found no blocker in the code. Two commits come after `a91eb11d3`:

- `30513c0bc` merges `main` at `deb5364ee`. Its remerge-diff is empty (class SAME).
- `3c3f13eb4` `fix(2d): the offset pass-start fallback warns`. The completeness-guard fallback note now carries the `RINGS_FALLBACK` marker (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/pass_start.rs:106-111`). The op posts one advisory `Warning::StrategyFallback` for each area that the start-side rings send to the Auto order (`crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs:3753-3759`). The pins are under "Pinning tests".

The refresh merges the current `main` (`64b737729`) into the branch. The merge commit is `f2a03d947`. Its remerge-diff is empty (class SAME). Only module lists auto-merged (`crates/app/src/operation/mod.rs`, `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests.rs`), and both sides keep their lines. No logic or safety rule changed. The delta review at `3c3f13eb4` stays valid, because only `main` merged since it.

## Readings

Shape-mask meter (`crates/motion/tests/common/shape_mask.rs`, widest cut along every planar feed; a full-width cut reads 8 mm), tool radius 4, step 4:
- The second read's band (stock 84 x 24, reach 100 x 40, round part radius 15), Outside: 7.966 mm on 59b42c727, 4.866 mm now. Uncut 0.000 mm2, no overcut into the part.
- The same band with a "Do not touch" pin, Outside: 7.966 mm on 59b42c727, 4.866 mm now; no avoid hit.
- Inside from an open bore (ring of stock 15..40): 8.000 mm on 59b42c727, 4.522 mm now.

fig8.step, EM-0800-4FL, Outside containment, the maintainer's heights: planar feed points with uncut stock on both flanks (`offset_pass_start/flanks.rs`): 8697 on 59b42c727, 0 now. The first ring of each level starts 4.000 mm outside the stock, and each level ends on the part wall.

Cost on fig8 (debug, motion only): Auto 9.5 s, 24768 moves, 18 lateral rapids; Outside 26.6 s, 25986 moves, 93 lateral rapids, 15 % more feed length (lead-ins and the lifts between pieces).

## Pinning tests (red on 59b42c727, green now)

- `camcraft-motion` `pass_start_levels` (new):
  - `outside_band_split_by_the_part_cuts_no_move_at_full_width` (red: 7.966 mm).
  - `outside_band_with_a_do_not_touch_pin_cuts_no_move_at_full_width` (red: 7.966 mm).
  - `inside_from_an_open_bore_cuts_no_move_at_full_width` (red: 8.000 mm).
  - `the_wall_first_and_narrow_cases_are_named_on_the_path` (new API).
  - `the_start_side_plan_posts_no_crossing_feeds` (new).
  - `the_stock_inside_a_ring_part_is_cut_whole` (red on 9939a6238: 153.7 mm2 left).
  - `a_pocket_with_a_hollow_boss_is_cut_whole` (red on 9939a6238: 1126 disallowed interior cells).
  - `the_wall_first_and_narrow_cases_are_named_on_the_path` now also pins the core note and the narrow note (a horseshoe part whose mouth is narrower than the tool).
- `camcraft-motion` lib `level_rings::guard_tests::the_guard_reads_a_standing_core_and_passes_a_whole_plan` (new).
- `camcraft-app` `offset_pass_start`:
  - `fig8_outside_offset_cuts_no_move_at_full_width` (red: 8697 points; heavy lane).
  - `fig8_outside_offset_starts_each_level_at_the_stock_edge` (heavy lane now).
  - `fig8_inside_offset_names_its_part_wall_start` (new).
  - `fig8_auto_offset_keeps_every_lateral_rapid_at_the_clearance_plane`, `mcp_sets_pass_start_refuses_an_unknown_word_and_undo_restores_it` (unchanged).
- `camcraft-geometry` lib `geo2d::clip_line::tests` (4).
- `camcraft-motion` lib `pass_start::tests::auto_says_nothing_and_each_wall_case_is_named`.
- `camcraft-ui` lib `egui_app::tests::pass_start::a_pass_start_warning_is_a_status_line` (new).

The two fig8 Outside tests take about 170 s each in debug (one generation and its verify), so they are in the app heavy lane.

- RINGS_FALLBACK pins (added in `3c3f13eb4`):
  - `camcraft-motion` lib `pass_start::tests::the_guard_fallback_is_an_offset_rings_fallback` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/pass_start.rs:134-146`). `rings_fallbacks` counts the guard note. It counts none of the other "Pass start" notes.

The only change after it is one warning note (`3c3f13eb4`). The two heavy steps that reach it are `app heavy: offset_pass_start` and `motion heavy: pass_start_levels`. They run at the cut gate.

Outside starts each level at the outer edge (with an Outside containment, outside the stock) and walks rings that follow that edge one stepover at a time, so the passes no longer slot the stock where the part splits the band. title: feat(cl): translate, XY turn, A/B turn and vertical mirror for toolpaths
body:
## What changed

- A new module `crates/cl/src/cl/transform.rs` with three sub-files (`transform_rotary.rs`, `transform_mirror.rs`, `transform_climb.rs`). `camcraft-app` re-exports it as `app::cl::transform`.
- `translate(tp, [dx, dy, dz])` shifts every move, arc center, canned cycle, compensated span and edge break.
- `transform_xy(tp, tx, ty, angle_deg, pivot)` turns the path in XY about a pivot and then shifts it. Nesting (#2166) can call it directly.
- `rotate_about_axis(tp, RotaryAxis::A | B, origin, angle_deg, chord_tol)` turns the path about X or Y. Each move states the turned tool axis. Arcs become chords within `chord_tol`, or return `ArcChordTolerance`.
- `mirror_plane(tp, MirrorPlane, MirrorMode)` mirrors the path across a vertical plane.
  - `GeometricMirror` gives the exact mirror image: G2 <-> G3 and G41 <-> G42.
  - `PreserveClimb(PassFamily)` mirrors and then runs each pass backwards between its entry and its retract. The lead-out becomes the lead-in. The arcs keep their original G2/G3, and the compensated spans keep their original side.
- `TransformError` names each refusal: `ThreadCycle`, `ProbeTouch`, `RotaryMove`, `TiltedMove`, `PlasmaCut`, `VerticalArc`, `CannedCycleTilt`, `ArcChordTolerance`, `HorizontalMirrorPlane`, `TiltedMirrorPlane`, `BadInput`, `NotReversible(why)`.
- The decisions are in `docs/decisions/3011-cl-transforms.md`.

## Cause

This is new work. The codebase had no shared transform for toolpaths. Patterns, mirror folders and nesting need one.

## Design

- All four transforms use one map, `p -> M p + t`, with `M` orthogonal.
- An arc keeps its plane only when `M` maps the plane normal exactly onto plus or minus itself. Its turn direction flips when `det(M)` times that sign is negative. This one rule gives the G2/G3 swap under a mirror. It also finds the XZ / YZ arcs that a transform cannot keep.
- Moves, arc centers and cycles snap to the coordinate lattice. Edge-break polylines do not snap, because a snap would move framed caps off orthonormal.
- `PreserveClimb` accepts only contour, profile and chamfer paths. It refuses these by name:
  - a helical ramp, adaptive clearing, multi-pass roughing and other families;
  - a ramp or helical entry;
  - a level change without a retract;
  - a cut before the first pass or after the last pass;
  - a link that is not on the clearance plane.

## Latest review fix

The latest review found that the arc sampler stops at 1,024 chords. A 1,000 mm semicircle exceeded the requested 0.0001 mm tolerance.

The rotary transform retains that bounded sampler. It samples at half the requested tolerance. It checks the curve error for the actual chord count and adds the endpoint rounding error. Circular arcs use the sagitta bound. Radius ramps use the sampler's second derivative bound. `ArcChordTolerance` refuses a path when the total bound exceeds `chord_tol`.

## Tests (pins)

The original 20 tests are in `crates/cl/src/cl/transform_tests.rs` and `transform_mirror_tests.rs` (`cargo test -p camcraft-cl --lib transform`):

- `translate_shifts_every_record_to_the_micron`, `translate_refuses_a_non_finite_offset`
- `transform_xy_turns_a_quarter_about_the_pivot_then_shifts`, `transform_xy_at_thirty_degrees_is_micron_accurate`, `transform_xy_refuses_a_vertical_arc_it_cannot_keep`
- `rotate_about_a_turns_the_point_and_states_the_axis`, `rotate_about_b_flattens_arcs_within_the_chord_tolerance`, `rotate_about_an_axis_by_zero_is_the_identity`, `rotate_about_an_axis_refuses_a_tilted_canned_cycle`
- `every_transform_refuses_thread_cycles_probe_touches_and_c_moves`
- `geometric_mirror_swaps_g2_g3_and_g41_g42`, `geometric_mirror_on_a_diagonal_plane_is_micron_accurate`, `mirror_refuses_horizontal_and_tilted_planes`, `mirror_refuses_tilted_moves`
- `preserve_climb_reverses_the_pass_between_entry_and_retract`, `preserve_climb_reverses_two_depths_linked_on_the_clearance_plane`, `preserve_climb_refuses_a_helical_entry`, `preserve_climb_refuses_clearing_families_by_name`, `preserve_climb_refuses_a_cut_before_the_first_pass`, `preserve_climb_refuses_a_level_change_without_a_retract`

The initial implementation report states that these pins did not compile before the API existed.

This round adds three pins:

- `rotate_about_a_refuses_an_arc_beyond_the_chord_budget`: refuses the review case. It also measures chord midpoint error on an accepted 1,000 mm semicircle.
- `rotate_about_b_bounds_arc_midpoints_in_each_plane`: measures analytic curve midpoint error in XY, XZ and YZ. It covers circular arcs, radius ramps, normal interpolation and both turn directions.
- `rotate_about_a_refuses_rounding_beyond_the_chord_tolerance`: refuses an arc whose endpoint rounding exceeds the tolerance.

Final head: `defb39c9c512312df3ee4723476bc284237b6e33`.

Pin proof for this round: the verifier saved the fixed rotary module outside the repository. Before the final commit, it restored the original module with:

```sh
git show a273ee018:crates/cl/src/cl/transform_rotary.rs > crates/cl/src/cl/transform_rotary.rs
CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache cargo test -j 24 -p camcraft-cl --lib rotate_about_
```

The new tests and error variant stayed in place. The result was RED: 5 passed and 2 failed. These pins failed:

- `rotate_about_a_refuses_an_arc_beyond_the_chord_budget`
- `rotate_about_a_refuses_rounding_beyond_the_chord_tolerance`

The verifier restored the fixed file and ran:

```sh
CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache cargo test -j 24 -p camcraft-cl --lib transform
```

The result was GREEN: all 23 transform tests passed.

The initial implementation report records these mutation results:

- the G2/G3 flip: 3 pins red
- the G41/G42 swap: 2 pins red
- the side restore in the climb reversal: 1 pin red
- the probe refusal: 1 pin red
- the refusal of a cut before the first pass: 1 pin red
- the horizontal-plane refusal: 1 pin red
- the pass reversal: 2 pins red
- the tilted-cycle refusal: 1 pin red

## Final validation

All final results cover head `defb39c9c512312df3ee4723476bc284237b6e33`.

At gate start, `upstream/main` was `deb5364eee89c57bef1388506cb3ea51b34c8776`. Another session advanced that shared ref during verification. At completion, it was `6e641dac753020bfed49fec310237eed28448141`. Both base commits have the same merge base with this head. The selected diff is unchanged.

- `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache cargo test -j 24 -p camcraft-cl --lib transform`: GREEN, 23 passed after restoration. The final-head quick CL library step passed all 69 tests.
- `CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1 CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=8 cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: GREEN, 1,077 steps, 0 failed, 52.4 minutes.
- `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache cargo clippy -j 8 -p camcraft-cl --all-targets -- -D warnings`: GREEN. Clippy for all selected crates also passed in quick.
- `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=24 cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: GREEN, 241 steps, 0 failed, 48.4 minutes. Registered known-fail steps behaved as expected.
- Quick step `app suites: example_catalog`: GREEN, 34 passed, 4 ignored. Heavy step `app heavy: example_catalog`: GREEN, the remaining 4 cases passed. All 38 catalog cases ran.
- Quick steps `app suites: example_catalog_adaptive` and `app suites: example_catalog_edge_work`: GREEN, 1 passed each.
- Reached golden step `app suites: golden_cl`: GREEN, 33 passed.

The first quick attempt stopped on a geometry build with E0463 after build artifact seeding. It ran 1 of 1,077 planned steps. The verifier removed only affected debug artifacts with `cargo clean --profile dev -p camcraft-kernel -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-cl`. The final retry disabled seeding and passed all 1,077 steps. No source change was required.

`git diff --check` passed. The worktree was clean at the final head.

UI checklist: not applicable. This PR changes no UI code or assets.

## Goldens moved

None. The catalog and reached golden suites ran. No recorded program changed or required regeneration.

## Not exercised

- No caller exists yet: patterns, mirror folders and nesting (#2166) will use it.
- No posted G-code goes through a transformed path in this PR.
- The framed edge-break caps under a turn and under a mirror are not pinned by a test.

All required validations completed. No UI screenshots were taken because this PR changes no UI. Existing untouched formatting fails a full touched-file rustfmt check. This round applies no broad reformat.

## Overlaps

#3046 adds a line to the module list of `crates/cl/src/cl/mod.rs` (the same file, but a different line). The PR that merges second refreshes.

Changelog: CL toolpath transforms: translate, XY turn, A/B axis turn and vertical-plane mirror (G2/G3 and G41/G42 swap, or a climb-preserving pass reversal), with named refusals.

Fixes #3011

title: feat(post): add RichAuto DSP A11 3-axis router post (.mmg format)
body:
## What changed

- New post `assets/posts/richauto.cps` for the RichAuto DSP A11 router controller.
- The post is registered as `"RichAuto DSP A11"` in `BUILTINS` (`crates/app/src/posting_files.rs`). It comes after Mach4, at the end of the mill posts.
- The output follows the `.mmg` program that a Laguna Swift A11 runs (#1907, comment of 2026-11-18). The comment of 2026-11-18 on this issue names that program as the conformance target.
  - The file extension is `.mmg`.
  - Each block has a sequence number: `N10`, then steps of 10. Comment lines and the `%` line have no number.
  - There are no spaces between words.
  - Lengths have three decimals. `F` is mm/min with one decimal.
  - Rapid is `G00` and feed is `G1`. The spindle starts with `M03S<rpm>` and stops with `M05`.
  - An axis word or an `F` word that does not change is not written.
  - The program ends with `M30` and then a `%` line.
- The setup block is `G21G90G17`. The post writes no `G54`, `G40`, `G80`, `G91.1`, `G94`, `G43`, `G49`, `T` or `M6` word.
- Offset 1 is the work origin that the operator sets on the pendant. Offsets 2 and higher are refused by name.
- Arcs use incremental `I`/`J`/`K` (`AbsCntr = Off`). An arc of more than 180 degrees is split.
- Drilling cycles are expanded to plain `G00`/`G1` moves, with the floor dwell and the bore spindle stop and restart.
- The `SpindleDwellMs` option writes `G04P<ms>` after the spindle start. The default is 0.
- The post refuses these by name: tapping, `G41`/`G42`, probing, rotary moves, `G96`, a second tool, an inch document, a bad rpm, a bad coolant, and a missing or low clearance plane.
- The post writes header notes (#2996) and WARN records as `(...)` comments.

## Cause

The shipped posts do not run safely on an A11. They write `G91.1`, `G53`, `T.. M6`, `G43` and canned cycles. A basic A11 firmware can refuse these words.

## Tests

- `crates/post/tests/script_richauto.rs` and `crates/post/tests/richauto_safety/mod.rs`: 41 tests, including the 11 recorded-stream goldens of `post_suite!`.
- The pin `richauto_writes_the_a11_mmg_block_format` was red on the older held script (format without `N`, `%`): `the program ends with %`. It is green on the new script.
- On `upstream/main` all the pins are red, because the post does not exist.
- `crates/app/tests/conformance.rs`: RichAuto is added to `POSTS`, `REFUSED` (`tap_plate`, "tapping"), the synth stream (G54, no tap) and `EXTENSIONS` (`mmg`). All 7 tests pass.
- `crates/post/tests/comment_escape.rs`: the count of shipped posts goes from 20 to 21.
- Mutations. Each mutant was run against the pins, then the script was restored and the pins were green again:
  - no final `%` line: 8 tests red, including `richauto_writes_the_a11_mmg_block_format`;
  - spaces between words: 18 tests red;
  - no modal word omission: 11 tests red, including `unchanged_axis_and_feed_words_are_left_out`;
  - no `onComment` hook: `comment_escape::header_notes_use_each_shipped_dialect_and_keep_the_full_surface_bound` red;
  - no sequence step (all blocks `N0`): 7 tests red.
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`, base `dfbe0d8a5`): 752 of 753 steps pass. The one red step is `slot_dxf_sketch::a_slot_outline_seeds_the_slot_and_cuts_it_to_size`. It fails in the same way on unchanged `upstream/main` (stale golden `slot_dxf_outline.cl`). I filed it as #3293.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Heavy lanes: not run.

## Goldens moved

- No existing golden changed.
- New: 12 conformance goldens in `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/richauto/`, `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/synth_richauto.nc`, and 11 recorded goldens in `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/richauto/` (6 programs, 5 refusals). I read each one. The arc centres are correct with a non-zero origin.

## Not exercised

- No program ran on an A11 or on the friend's Laguna Swift.
- The A11 response to `G21G90G17`, to `G2`/`G3` with incremental centres and to `G04P` is not confirmed. The sample program has no setup block, no arcs and no dwell.
- The sample program has CRLF line ends. This post writes LF.
- `axisInversion` is not declared. The engine refuses a machine with an inverted axis by name. Grbl 1.1 is the same.

## Overlaps

These open PRs add rows to the same lists (`BUILTINS`, or the lists in `conformance.rs`). They touch other posts and do not change the same function: #3160, #3058, #2999, #2993, #2992, #2981, #2979, #2978, #2974, #2972, #2969, #2968, #2964, #2955, #2951, #2646, #2515. The PR that merges second refreshes.

Changelog: New built-in post "RichAuto DSP A11" for RichAuto A11 routers (Laguna Swift, Grizzly): .mmg files with N numbers, one tool, drilling as plain moves, named refusals for tapping, cutter compensation and probing.

Fixes #1914

title: fix(post): block cutting tools at reserved numbers and names
body:
## What changed

Machine files accept `tooling.reserved` entries.
Each entry reserves a number, a name, or both for `probe` or `tool_setter`.
The reader and validator refuse malformed entries by key.
Stored projects retain the reservations.

New cutting tools skip reserved numbers.
A probe takes a declared probe pocket.
Tool edits and library imports refuse incompatible reserved numbers or names.
Verification and posting also refuse old unsafe assignments.
The existing GUI, script, and MCP commands use these checks.
Tool number zero remains refused.

The standalone post CLI checks its input before it creates or replaces output.
It retains the loaded tool across sections.
A new TOOL needs its own declared kind.
A stream with no tool selector cannot post motion on a machine with reservations.
Indexed lookups keep the checks bounded for long streams.

A machine that omits the field reserves nothing.
No shipped machine file reserves a pocket in this PR (see "Review round 2").

body:
## Stock safety fix (current round)

Final head: `ebe55a46f01c774fbdcdcdd49f05205cfb8ec550`.

Multi-Axis Deburr now requires the complete stock boundary to match the source mesh.
Generation and posting refuse missing, empty, non-finite or different stock by name.
The comparison sorts triangle vertices and triangles. It ignores ordering, normals and winding.
Equal bounds do not satisfy the check.

For matching stock, the existing source guard checks the cone, flute, shank and holder through the cut, entry and exit.
Generation also runs the shared `plunge_solid::audit_posed` check.
Posting reads the live stock before it accepts a cached path.
The refusal also applies to a safe different tessellation or stock removed by an earlier operation.
The column simulator still does not judge posed moves. The named refusal prevents an unproved stock verdict from permitting posting.

Pins in `mcp_multiaxis_deburr`:

- `multiaxis_deburr_refuses_stock_beside_the_vertical_edge`.
- `multiaxis_deburr_rechecks_stock_before_posting_the_cached_path`.
- `multiaxis_deburr_live_stock_judge_refuses_an_unjudged_cached_path`.

The clear controls first generate and post source-shaped stock.
The unsafe case adds 60 x 60 x 10 mm stock beside a 40 x 40 x 10 mm part.
The generation pin also sets `center_cutting=true` to isolate the complete-tool guard from the plunge check.
The cached-post pin checks the actual post command after a stock edit. Freshness refuses it and no NC file is written.
The direct live-judge pin checks the named stock refusal independently of freshness.

Pin proof:

- Removing only the generation stock guard makes `multiaxis_deburr_refuses_stock_beside_the_vertical_edge` fail. Generation returns `status: ok`.
- Removing only the live stock guard makes `multiaxis_deburr_live_stock_judge_refuses_an_unjudged_cached_path` fail. The judge returns `None`.
- Restoring both source files byte for byte makes all nine `mcp_multiaxis_deburr` tests pass.

`CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test -p camcraft-app --test mcp_multiaxis_deburr` passed all nine tests on the final head.

Final-head quick gate:

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed all 526 steps in 75.3 minutes.
The run had zero failures and zero stalls. It used the merged main revision `deb5364ee`.
Motion library: 551 passed, 10 ignored. App library: 297 passed.
UI library: 1434 passed, 8 ignored. MCP suite: nine passed.
`slot_dxf_sketch`: four passed. No reached golden changed.
The shared `upstream/main` reference advanced to `ef157211` during the run. The tested tree did not change.

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed on the final head in 1 minute 31 seconds.

Final-head heavy gate:

`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` passed all 244 steps in 58.4 minutes.
The reached lanes were `motion heavy` and `app heavy`. The run had zero failures and zero stalls.
All 108 ordinary ignored tests passed. All four known-fail checks matched their expected failures.
The heavy `example_catalog` suite passed all four tests.
The command used the current `upstream/main` reference after its advance to `ef157211`.
The tested head remained `ebe55a46f01c774fbdcdcdd49f05205cfb8ec550`.

Catalog and goldens on the final head:

- `app suites: example_catalog`: 37 passed, 4 ignored, zero failures.
- `app suites: example_catalog_adaptive`: one test passed.
- `app suites: example_catalog_edge_work`: one test passed.
- Goldens moved: none. The catalog suites ran. No recorded program changed in this fix.

The branch includes a clean merge of main as fetched at this round's start: `deb5364ee`.
No conflict required a hand edit. `PROCESS_VERSION` comes from main.
The new exhaustive `pick_kinds` match receives the same `NotTaken(PICK_OWED)` arm as Deburr.
This merge compatibility fix permits the requested current-main build.
This round changes no UI. The existing screenshots still show the current controls.

Changelog: Multi-Axis Deburr refuses stock that lacks a complete posed-tool clearance proof, including changed stock at post.

The earlier sections below record their stated heads. Their validation does not replace this round's validation.

## Separate-part safety fix (earlier round)

Head: `91a03dd8c9d000effb3f4510bd325495a6d22d05`.

Multi-Axis Deburr now refuses by name when another kept part exists. Generation collects the other parts through the shared keep law. Posting checks the live parts before it accepts a cached path. The other parts receive no chamfer exemption. Edge selection stays on the source. This conservative refusal also applies to distant kept parts.

Pins in `mcp_multiaxis_deburr`:
- `multiaxis_deburr_refuses_regeneration_with_a_separate_kept_part`.
- `multiaxis_deburr_rechecks_a_separate_part_before_posting_the_cached_path`.

Each pin uses the review's separate cube and first generates and posts the clear source. The suite passed 6/6. Removing the generation guard, the live posting guard, or the keep-law entry failed the corresponding pins. Each restored source passed. Removing the keep-law entry reproduced the unsafe cached post.

Final-head validation:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 515/516 passed. Only the previously reported stale Slot golden failed in `slot_dxf_sketch::a_slot_outline_seeds_the_slot_and_cuts_it_to_size`. No golden changed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: 242/242 passed. Reached lanes: `motion heavy` and `app heavy`. All 102 ordinary ignored tests passed. All six expected-failure checks matched.

## What changed

- A new operation kind, **Multi-Axis Deburr** (`OpType::MultiAxisDeburr`), is appended at ordinal 46 in `Section::MultiAxis`. Stored kind ids do not move.
- It has every field of the 3D Deburr and five more: `axis_mode` (`Axis5` / `Axis4`), `lead_deg`, `lag_deg`, `max_tilt_deg` and `shank_avoid`.
- New kernel `camcraft_motion::multiaxis::multiaxis_deburr` (`deburr_axis.rs`, `deburr_pose.rs`):
  - The tool lays one cone flank on the chamfer plane of each break. The cut is the flat chamfer for every pose that turns the axis about the plane normal.
  - `Axis5` leans the axis inside `max_tilt_deg`. `Axis4` keeps the axis square to the A axis (about X).
  - Mandatory continuous facet checks cover the full cone and the supplied physical shank and holder. They cover each complete cut, entry and exit. The stored `shank_avoid` option cannot disable this guard.
  - An edge with no clear pose follows the Deburr's unreachable-edge policy: skip with a note, or refuse by name.
  - The tool enters and leaves along a checked, bounded axis line. The entire cone stays above `bottom_z`. Pose changes, gaps and chamfer-plane corners split runs.
  - Each run declares a framed flat `EdgeBreak` cap (#1891).
- The exposed-edge scan moved from `finishing3d/deburr.rs` into the shared `finishing3d/deburr_scan.rs`. The 3D Deburr calls it in the same order.
- App wiring: kind row, seed, sanity door (lead minus lag inside the cap), generate arm, cache stamp, project DTO (`multi_axis_deburr`), heights, setup sheet, section mode, WCS refusals, sim break bound.
- MCP: `add_operation`, `edit_operation` and `set_operation_geometry` work with the new kind through the generic tools.
- UI: `multiaxis_deburr_page.rs` (Geometry: size, filters, unreachable policy; Passes: axis mode, lean, max tilt, shank avoid; Heights; Feeds). The kind has its own original glyph (`assets/ui/svg/op-multiaxis-deburr.svg`, PNG from `cargo xtask icons`).

## Cause

New feature (#1894). A vertical cone cannot break steep or vertical edges, so the 3D Deburr skips them.

## UI screenshots

The before images show revision `971c23faa026865be47e425a660439f8c3d17ecd`, an ancestor of this PR's base. The new kind is absent there.
The after images show the original feature head `c2560be2bc4f8900f5cc238bb5879742ff8169d5`. The safety fixes below do not change the UI.
These are actual application window captures. They show the operation controls and entry. They do not show generated toolpaths.
The images are stored only on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch, commit `849e3eeba9e01f8f2ce72691074d81ab12b27775`.

The new Passes page shows the axis mode, lead, lag, tilt cap and shank avoidance controls.

## Safety review fixes on the new head

Final head: `a312b20ebdb48c2505ec417c6008d5cc1c6569d4`.

- Each candidate trims the edge until the tip and the lowest cone-rim point stay at or above `bottom_z` on every pass.
- Continuous outer convex polyhedra enclose the cone and the physical tool bands along the entire cutting segment.
- Facet clipping permits cone and cutting-flute contact only within the finite requested chamfer prism. Floors, other faces and material past an edge end receive no exemption.
- The same continuous checks cover the complete entry and exit lines. Clearance endpoints must put the whole tool above the part. The first plunge stages the axis change above every part face plus the largest tool radius and 1 mm.
- An axis that is too flat or requires more than 100 tool diameters of reach is refused. Unsafe segments use the existing named skip or refuse policy.
- The app supplies the physical shank and holder even when `shank_avoid` is false. The kernel guards the operation because column stock simulation does not judge posed cuts.

Regression pins:

- `the_brick_keeps_the_tilted_tip_and_entire_cone_above_the_bottom`: complete cone and tip stay above the brick's programmed bottom; clear vertical edges still cut.
- `a_raised_bottom_clips_the_cone_without_a_part_floor_to_hide_the_error`: a raised window isolates the bottom guard from the part floor.
- `a_boss_on_a_floor_skips_the_unsafe_foot_and_still_cuts_the_clear_edge`: the window extends below the floor; the unsafe foot is skipped and the clear upper edge still cuts.
- `an_obstacle_on_the_entry_line_is_skipped_while_clear_edges_still_cut`: an obstacle away from the cut blocks the entry or exit; other edges still cut.
- `an_unsafe_entry_refuses_by_name_when_skipping_is_disabled`: the picked edge cuts without the obstacle and refuses with the obstacle.
- `disabling_shank_avoid_cannot_bypass_the_mandatory_holder_collision_guard`: the option is off; an obstacle that misses the cone and shank still blocks the holder.

Mutation checks (each restored byte for byte):

- Ignored the pose offset in bottom clipping: the raised-window pin failed with a cone below `bottom_z`. Restored: passed.
- Disabled cone facet checks: the boss-floor pin failed with a cone in the floor. Restored: passed.
- Checked only the cut and omitted the entry/exit sweeps: the entry-obstacle pin failed when the tip crossed the obstacle. Restored: passed.
- Omitted the physical shank and holder from the app adapter: the option-off holder pin failed. Restored: passed.
- Sent the first plunge directly to the tip: the existing MCP generation pin failed with two mid-turn shank findings. Restored: passed.

- The final commit removes one redundant `let` binding. It does not change the guarded geometry or the tests.
- Final-head quick selection: `motion suites: lib` and `app suites: mcp_multiaxis_deburr` passed both steps in 1.9 minutes. Motion: 530 passed, 10 ignored. MCP: 4 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed on the exact final source tree.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` passed all 242 steps on the final head in 40.9 minutes. The reached lanes were `motion heavy` and `app heavy`. All 102 ordinary ignored tests passed. All six registered known-fail checks matched their expected failures.
- All 13 `multiaxis::deburr_axis_tests` passed in release mode on the final head. This includes all five new kernel safety pins.

The recorded gate runs used `CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1`. An earlier run with incompatible build artifacts was excluded. No golden, screenshot, log or review image is part of these fix commits.

title: feat(wire): export a selected Agie opening for zero-step inspection
body:
The DXF import and Wire Contour selection prerequisites merged in #3193 and #3205. This PR adds the native zero-step inspection export.

The maintainer confirmed that the dependency and Agie-CAM reference approvals from #2951 also apply here. This PR gets its own safety review and trial-merge test after #2951 merges. [Maintainer decision](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/3219#issuecomment-7080044891)

## Change

Use `camcraft-cli export-agie-inspection <project> <operation> <new-directory>` for a saved operation.

A user can create an unassigned wire inspection operation on the Post page and choose one placed, closed DXF chain and an internal start. The user can save the operation and export a native Classic Cut 2S ISO/SBR/SBL directory with zero working steps. The CLI and MCP use the same entry points.

The exporter preserves the nominal line and circular arc geometry. It checks the source selection, closure, winding, rounding, arc extrema, start disk and supported mounted machine axes. It refuses a changed or unsuitable selection and a destination that exists. An inspection work does not become a qualified machining operation.

This first setup uses 10 mm height, a 3 mm internal start and a 0.25 mm wire. The reference piece has unknown physical X/Y dimensions. Its controller fields store zero length and breadth. The receipt identifies the unverified fixture, erosion settings, physical Z and perpendicular controller lead. It describes the controller’s quality request separately from an assigned erosion process. The nominal setup does not promise a historical start seam, lead or cut sequence.

## Verification on the refreshed head

Commit `d982d452b` merges upstream main at `4e0c81964` into the contributor branch. The only manual resolution was the generated MCP reference. The compiled registry and the published reference list the same 119 tools. A trial merge with main at `6308a5db5` completed without conflicts.

The targeted author check passed 104 tests on this head. These covered post (6), MCP (3), desktop (3), application regressions (74) and geometry (18). Strict all-target Clippy passed for the four touched crates. The complete quick selector listed 1,048 steps. The author ran the targeted quick alternative.

The refreshed CLI imported an unchanged drawing, reopened the saved operations and exported two native jobs. All six files matched the controller-checked files byte for byte. Each receipt reported zero working steps. Repeat exports refused to overwrite either job.

The official heavy gate passed all 254 selected steps in 62.7 minutes on this revision. The command exited with status 0.

```sh
cargo xtask gate heavy --base 4e0c81964
```

## Earlier verification on `d13c5eed1`

Contributor head: `d13c5eed15251af0a903396c1d96bba298b644d0`. Parent: `2d0fa64841a1b42dbacb330f75f6bab61897da10`.

All eight scoped tests passed on this earlier head: two post tests, three MCP tests and three desktop tests. Strict all-target Clippy passed for geometry, post, app and UI. The independent synthetic export preserved every directed edge, arc center and resource link. It wrote one start, one work and zero steps. The checks include:

- `agie_inspection_accepts_listed_chain_and_checks_mounted_travel_in_the_wcs`
- `saved_selected_opening_exports_zero_steps_through_the_desktop_action`
- `unassigned_inspection_opening_survives_undo_redo_and_project_reopen`
- `setup_post_inspection_fields_and_submit_fit_the_visible_panel`

On this earlier revision, 252 of 253 heavy steps passed. The bulk release build failed to link two test binaries when the device ran out of space. The refreshed revision has its own gate run.

The desktop authoring and selection use a real undoable operation. The documented MCP reference was regenerated from the compiled CLI. The public selection returned by `list_features` can be passed directly to `create_agie_inspection`. A regression narrows the mount travel and reverses an axis. Each case refuses before file creation.

We used an offline VM running a copy of the actual Agie Classic Cut 2S control. The control opened native files produced by CAMCraft. We checked the program and ISO identities, nominal orientation, hole size and position, setup height, zero separation and zero working steps. Each work-level formal check blocked on undefined working technology. Each whole-piece check also flagged the low zero X/Y dimensions. Both control previews rendered the bound nominal profiles. An identical repeat import with the quality already present kept zero assigned working steps. Repeating an export to the same directory preserved the old files. No physical cut was made.

No model data, original job or simulator software is included. The public geometry tests are original synthetic cases. This inspection slice does not qualify a working erosion process, a physical slug restraint or an automatic cutting release. #3178 remains open for qualified curved die cutting. #3179 retains its physical process requirements.

## Desktop comparison

Both images use the same synthetic project and 750 by 830 pixel setup panel. The parent has the existing post controls. The new form shows the selected opening, wire and both start coordinates.

| Parent | This change |
| --- | --- |
| ![Parent setup Post panel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/69865cfd9c4856f159fd63c5ba79b7b08724e264/issue-3179/setup-before.png) | ![Setup Post panel with the Agie inspection form](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/69865cfd9c4856f159fd63c5ba79b7b08724e264/issue-3179/setup-after.png) |

Effort: high. No escalation.

title: feat(import): state the STEP length unit, and ask for it when the file has none
body: ## What changed A STEP model import states the length unit that the model was read in. A STEP file that states no length unit is never read in a guessed unit. - **Kernel** (`crates/kernel/src/step_assumed_unit.rs`, `solidcore_step.rs`, `solidcore_step_import.rs`): `read_step_assuming` and `import_step_model_assuming` take the caller's millimetres per unit. For a file whose contexts state no length unit, the unit is written into each representation context before the read. The tolerance, the edge-gap cap and the chord are then in the same unit as the geometry. A file that states its own unit keeps it. A stated size outside 0.001..=1000 mm is refused by name. - **Geometry** (`crates/geometry/src/step.rs`): `parse_open_assuming`. A file with no length unit and no caller unit is `StepError::MissingUnits`. `StepMesh` carries `length_units_mm` and `assumed_mm`. - **App**: - `ImportError::StepUnitsMissing`. - `ImportModel::within_in` and `from_bytes_in`, and the unit option on each import path: the file, the bytes, the sourced load and the cadmpeg conversion. - A unit for a file that is not STEP is refused by name before parsing, as a facet budget is. - The last import note names the unit: `length unit: in (stated by the file)`, `length unit: in (stated at import; the file states no length unit)`, or `... (stated by the file; the in stated at import is not used)`. - **MCP and script**: `import_model` takes `units` (`"mm"` or `"in"`). `cam.import` takes it as the fourth argument. `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` and `assets/scripts/cam.d.ts` are regenerated. - **UI**: a refused unitless import opens the **Length unit** modal (`egui_app/step_units_prompt.rs`), with the buttons Millimeters (mm), Inches (in) and Cancel. The answer goes through the command queue (`CommandKind::ResolveStepUnits`) and runs the same import again. The import that lands is one undoable command. Cancel and Escape import nothing. An import-as-fixture binding is kept for the second import. - **Docs**: `units-and-coordinates.md` (it said that a unitless STEP file "is kept as millimetres") and a new `troubleshooting.md` entry. The decision record is `docs/decisions/1874-step-length-units.md`. ## Screenshot The Length unit prompt for a STEP file that states no length unit (the status line under it says the same): ## Decisions (see the decision record) - The file's own unit wins over the caller's (the DXF import does the reverse, #1862). A STEP unit context is an exact statement of the CAD system. - The chosen unit is not recorded on the model. A linked-file re-import asks again. - Tool holders, fixtures and tool bodies from a unitless STEP file are refused by name, with no prompt. ## Pinning tests - `camcraft-kernel` `step_assumed_unit` (3): a unitless box reads 25.4² times the area in inches; the file's own unit wins; an out-of-range unit is refused by name. - `camcraft-app` `step_units_import` (5): the typed refusal; the inch and mm imports and their notes; the file's mm, in and m notes; a unit for an STL is refused; MCP `import_model` with no unit, a bad unit and `in`. - `camcraft-ui` lib `step_units_tests` (5): the question, the answer as one undoable import (inch is 25.4 times the mm width), Cancel, and no question for a file that states its unit. - `camcraft-ui` lib `egui_app::tests::step_units_prompt` (4): the labels, no prompt without a question, a unit button, Cancel and Escape. - Updated, because each STEP import now ends with the unit note: `import_step_outward` (3 tests) and `import_step_closed_shell` `a_flipped_face_is_named_in_the_import_result_and_the_mcp_answer`. They assert the unit note in place of "no notes". No assertion is weaker. ## Gates Final head b5637db2b (the review fixes on 2649bb17e), Windows x86_64, without sccache: - Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): 1033 steps, 1032 ok. The one red step is `ai_guide_calls_match_live_tools_list`, the CRLF defect #3119, which this PR does not touch. - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean (kernel and geometry on 2649bb17e; they did not change after it). - Heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`): `kernel heavy` (17 steps), `motion heavy` (37 steps) and `app heavy` (198 steps), after one release build. 253 steps ok, 0 failed, 26.1 min. The known-fail steps of #1950 and #2849 are red as expected. (The run on 2649bb17e also had 253 steps ok.) - Note: with `RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache`, two gate runs here failed with "can't find crate" (`num_enum`, then `flecs_ecs`) and the warning `ignoring -C extra-filename flag due to -o flag`. The runs without sccache are correct. This is a local cache matter, not this change. ## Review fixes (b5637db2b) - `crates/app/tests/cadmpeg_import.rs`: the eight `load_open_within` calls in the `#[cfg(unix)]` module pass `None` for the new `units` argument. This module does not compile on Windows, so it is not in the Windows gates above. It needs a build on Linux or macOS. - `State::take_step_units`: each import start takes the chosen unit, whatever its file. A unit never waits for a later import of the same file. Pinned by `step_units_tests::a_chosen_unit_never_waits_for_a_later_import_of_the_same_file`. - `troubleshooting.md`: the answer is not kept; the next import, a linked file's re-import included, asks again. ## Not exercised - A unitless file from the cadmpeg converter was not tried. That path uses the same `parse_model_open_in`. - `crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs` and `crates/app/src/script/api.rs` were already over 400 lines. They grow by 2 and 7 lines. Changelog: A STEP import states the model's length unit, and a STEP file that states no unit is no longer read as millimetres: the desktop app asks for mm or inches, and MCP and scripts take `units` (#1874) Fixes #1874 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: feat(ui): load machine and post files from the user's disk in the browser
body:
## What changed

The browser build now loads the user's own machine (`.mch`) and post (`.cps`) files. The bytes come from the browser, not from a path.

- **Load machine (.mch)** and **Load post (.cps)** are live in the browser. They open the browser file picker. A picked machine is mounted. A picked post is selected.
- The Machine page has a new button **Load folder (.mch, .cps)** in the browser build only. It opens `<input webkitdirectory multiple>`. It adds each `.mch` and `.cps` file of the folder to the session lists. It does not need the File System Access API.
- A drop with a `.mch` or `.cps` file goes to a new module `setup_file_drop`. One file is mounted or selected. Several files only join the lists. One status line counts the files that landed and names each refused file with its reason.
- On the desktop, one dropped `.mch` or `.cps` on disk goes to `LoadMachineFile` or `SelectPostFile` by its full path.
- The domain module `camcraft_post::session_files`, re-exported by app, keeps each file by its bare name for the session, on the thread that loaded it. The caller passes app machine validation and holder-aware parsing as a callback. A file enters it only when it passes the checks of a file from disk: a machine must validate and parse, a post must compile and run.
- The readers of machine and post files consult the session store first, then the disk. So `LoadMachineFile`, `SelectPostFile` and the MCP tools run unchanged. Each mount and post choice stays one undo step.
- Session machines show in the machine catalogue (`library::enumerate`). Session posts show in the post combo list.
- A saved project that names a session file which is not loaded again is refused by that name (#2319). There is no fallback.

## Cause

The browser build had no disk and no picker for these files. `browser_files::refusal` greyed Load machine and Load post with `NEEDS_PICKER`. The file drop took model files only. The readers of `PostRef::File` and the machine file read only from disk.

## Tests

Pins in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/browser_setup_files.rs`:

- `a_dropped_mch_mounts_by_its_name_and_one_undo_takes_it_away`
- `a_dropped_cps_is_selected_and_posts_from_its_bytes`
- `several_dropped_files_land_and_each_bad_one_is_refused_by_name`
- `a_malformed_pick_is_refused_by_name_and_changes_nothing`
- `a_picked_folder_fills_both_lists_and_a_picked_file_mounts_or_selects`
- `the_machine_and_post_load_buttons_are_live_in_the_browser` (AccessKit label, role `Button`, enabled state for "Load machine (.mch)", "Load folder (.mch, .cps)" and "Load post (.cps)"; no folder button on the desktop)

Other tests:

- `session_files::tests::a_bad_file_is_refused_by_name_and_never_kept` (post unit test). `an_unloaded_session_post_is_refused_by_name_at_post_time` pins a project that names a file that is not loaded.
- `setup_file_drop::tests::one_file_is_for_its_own_kind_in_any_case`.
- Updated for the new law: `browser_files::tests::every_picker_and_folder_command_is_refused_by_name_in_the_browser`, `a_picker_the_browser_lacks_is_refused_by_name_not_ignored`, `a_file_button_is_greyed_with_its_reason_in_the_browser`.

Red before the fix (reduced pins on unchanged `upstream/main`):

- the drop pins failed with `drop refused: drop-2950-vmc.mch is not a model file (read: .stl, .obj, .step, .stp, .sc, .solidcraft)`;
- the button pin failed with `LoadMachineDialog runs the browser's picker` / `left: Some("Not available in the browser yet: ...")`.

Mutation checks (old code put back, pins run, code restored):

- `crates/ui/src/browser_files.rs` from upstream: `the_machine_and_post_load_buttons_are_live_in_the_browser` red.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/shell.rs` from upstream (drop route not called): the three drop pins red.
- `crates/app/src/posting.rs` from upstream (no session read at post time): `a_dropped_cps_is_selected_and_posts_from_its_bytes` red.
- `session_files::add_post` without its compile check: `several_dropped_files_land_and_each_bad_one_is_refused_by_name` red.
- All pins green again after each restore.

Gate:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` ran all 428 steps on the previous head. 427 passed. `ui suites: lib` failed in three machines-pane tests. The cause was a process-global store: the session machines of the new tests leaked into the machine list of tests on other threads.
- The fix makes the store thread-local. The browser runs on one thread.
- On the final head, `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main --only "app suites: lib" --only "ui suites: lib"` is green (ui lib 1385 passed, 0 failed). Only `crates/app/src/session_files.rs` changed between the two heads, plus one test comment and the decision file. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- The wasm32 build. The `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target is not installed on this machine, so the wasm-only code was not compiled. That code is: the folder input and batch read in `file_pick.rs`, the async drop read in `setup_file_drop.rs`, and the dialog openers in `state_picked.rs`. A reviewer with the target must run `cargo check -p camcraft-ui --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
- A real browser. The tests use `State::browser_build` and in-memory drops as the stand-in.
- Persistence in IndexedDB. Not built. The decision file lists the options for the maintainer.

## Overlaps

- #3057 changes `file_drop::take_drop`. This PR does not change that function. It adds `setup_file_drop::take`, which `shell.rs` calls before `take_drop`. Whichever merges second refreshes.
- Several open PRs touch `crates/app/src/posting.rs` and `crates/ui/src/state.rs` in other functions. This PR changes only `script_of`, `resolve_cps` (one line each), the `LoadMachineDialog` / `SelectPostDialog` arms and one new `CommandKind` variant.

## MCP

No new MCP tool. The browser routes go through the existing `LoadMachineFile` and `SelectPostFile` commands, and the MCP machine and post tools read the session store through the same readers. `LoadSetupFolderDialog` is a browser-only picker. It changes no document state.

Decision file: `docs/decisions/2950-browser-machine-post-files.md`.

Effort: high

Changelog: The browser build loads your own machine (.mch) and post (.cps) files from a picker, a folder picker or a drop; a bad file is refused by name.

Fixes #2950

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


## Review fixes

- A different post under an existing name is refused. Identical text is accepted. `same_name_folder_and_picker_leave_the_selected_post_and_history_stable` pins the selected post and history.
- One browser batch has a 32 MiB raw-byte limit. Both file lists share a 32 MiB retained-name-and-text limit. Refusals name the file. `individually_allowed_files_cannot_exceed_the_batch_budget` and `retained_text_budget_covers_both_lists_and_refuses_by_name` pin the limits.
- A successful machine import invalidates the machine catalogue. `a_folder_machine_import_invalidates_the_populated_catalogue` starts with a populated catalogue and pins the refreshed list.
- Pure storage and readers belong to `camcraft-post`. App supplies its existing machine checks through a callback. `pure_session_readers_are_available_without_the_app` pins the domain API.

## Machine and Post page images

These images show the shipped pages through the native render harness with the browser flag enabled. They are not browser captures.
Before uses the actual PR parent page and browser refusal code. After uses the review fix source.
The capture checks that the old load buttons are disabled, the new load buttons are enabled, and the folder button appears.
The files exist only on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch.

| Page | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Machine | ![Machine before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/3160/machine-before.png) | ![Machine after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/3160/machine-after.png) |
| Post | ![Post before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/3160/post-before.png) | ![Post after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/3160/post-after.png) |

## Heavy lanes

Validated unchanged head `5e7c2b0d006c543316df6c062608aa2969c01722` on 2026-11-22.
The run used freshly fetched `upstream/main` at `148a5c832aa811bab9cae5c7f69e0ad945ee92d4`.
The shared base reference advanced to `ef157211438104997fc9e51f7e3affc4db303545` during execution. This result records the starting base.

- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: GREEN, exit 0; 199 steps, 0 failed steps; 45.7 minutes.
- `cargo xtask gate batch --only "app suites: example_catalog"`: GREEN, exit 0; 1 step; 33 tests passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored.
- The heavy `example_catalog` step ran both ignored catalog tests. Both passed.
- No goldens changed. No source files changed. No new commit or push was needed.

The heavy gate accepted four registered expected failures. These are not new failures:

- #2849: `an_axis_aligned_lead_start_posts_the_users_arc_entry_as_g18_or_g19`.
- #2849: `the_horizontal_arc_entry_on_the_users_pocket_verifies_silent`.
- #2849: `fig8_outside_containment_with_em0800_and_clearing_kinds_works`.
- #1950: `the_users_whole_model_bore_roughs_adaptive_on_each_level`.

This round runs the checks owed by the clean review of this head. It adds no code fix or new mutation check.
The earlier review records the quick gate, clippy, and mutation results. This round does not repeat those checks.

title: feat(ui): show the operator side at the work envelope
body:
## What changed

The viewport now shows the operator side of the work envelope. An arrow starts at the lower edge of the operator-side face. The arrow points out of the envelope, toward the operator. The text "Operator side" is at the tip of the arrow.

- `camcraft-post`: a machine file can state `general.operator_side`. The words are `"-X"`, `"+X"`, `"-Y"` and `"+Y"`. The word names the world axis that points from the envelope to the operator.
  - The field is optional. Old machine files and old projects load without a change.
  - A wrong word refuses the file by name. A wrong word never reads as the default.
  - `OperatorSide::default_for` gives the default of each machine kind: `+Y` for a lathe, `-Y` (the front) for each other kind.
- `camcraft-ui`: `operator_side.rs` builds the arrow when its input changes (the placed envelope and the side). Each other frame reads the kept arrow. The text is screen text, so it stays readable when the view turns.
- The View door has a new box, "Show operator side". It is view state: on by default, no command, not saved. It is disabled while the work envelope is off.
- The arrow and the text use the envelope colour. They are outside the envelope, so they do not cover the part or the toolpath.
- Docs: `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` (the machine file grammar) and `docs/decisions/2632-operator-side.md` (the defaults for each kind).

## Cause

This is new work that the maintainer asked for. The viewport did not show from which side the operator looks into the work envelope.

## Before and after screenshots

Both captures use the seeded shell at 1280 × 720 with the HAAS VF-2 machine file mounted and the work envelope shown. The camera looks from the front. "Before" is the same scene with the new box off. With the box off, the scene is the same as on `upstream/main`.

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/716acb4411ebb971886b4c98b17eeeb805770f76/2632/operator-side-before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/716acb4411ebb971886b4c98b17eeeb805770f76/2632/operator-side-after.png) |

The screenshots are only on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch. A temporary collector made them. The collector is not in this branch.

title: feat(motion): Bore gets a Helical strategy (one helix to the floor, then a floor circle)
body:
## What changed

- New `BoreStrategy` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/bore_helix.rs`): `Rings` (the level ladder, the default and every earlier bore) or `Helical { spring_pass }`. `BoreParams` and `OpParams::Bore` get the field `strategy`.
- A helical hole has these moves:
  1. A rapid over the helix start at the clearance height.
  2. A rapid down to the plunge height over the material.
  3. One continuous helix on the wall radius (`rc = R - r - leave`, the same circle as the last ring) to the floor.
  4. One flat floor circle. With `spring_pass`, a second floor circle.
  5. A feed to the centre at the floor, then a rapid up to clearance.
  
  A through hole's helix ends at the floor less the break-through. The helix is arcs of at most half a turn, so each arc posts as one G2/G3 with Z.
- The pitch is `stepdown`. The Heights tab calls it "Helix pitch" for a helical Bore. Climb is CCW, as for the rings.
- Two refusals in `BoreParams::validate`, before any move is built:
  - A hole that one helix cannot clear to the centre (`rc > floor reach`). For a flat end mill, the limit is twice the tool diameter. The message gives the core and the widest hole.
  - A helix steeper than 15 deg. The message gives the largest pitch that fits.
- Detect holes (`crates/app/src/operation/bore_reach.rs`) skips, and names, the holes that one helix cannot clear when the Bore is helical.
- Project file: `helical` and `spring_pass` on the `bore` record, written only when true. A ring ladder writes the same JSON as before. No version step (see the decision file).
- Stamp: the digest writes the strategy only for a helical Bore. A ring ladder keeps the stamp that it had.
- MCP: `list_operation_types` lists `helical` and `spring_pass` for `bore`. A params patch sets them.
- UI (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/holes_page.rs`): a Strategy combo and a Spring pass check on the Passes tab, the "Helix pitch" label on the Heights tab, and a Lead-in hint that the level links do not apply.
- Guide: a "Helical strategy" part in the Bore section of `site/content/guide/operations/operations-2d.md`, and two rows in `site/content/guide/reference/refusals.md`.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/2830-helical-bore.md`.
- Mechanical: each `BoreParams` and `OpParams::Bore` literal in the tests gets `strategy: Default::default()` (the ring ladder).

## Readings

The issue's counterbore, posted with `assets/posts/linuxcnc.cps`. The model is a revolved block with a Ø11 x 7 recess at the origin (top Z0). The tool is EM-0600-4FL (Ø6 flat), with a 1 mm pitch, climb, clearance 10 and retract 5. A scratch test built the document with the commands, then called `posting::post_script`. It is not committed. The status is Ok and the post has no warning. The cutting part of the program:

```
G0 Z10
G0 X2.5 Y0
G0 X2.5 Y0 Z10
G0 X2.5 Y0 Z2
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z1.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z1 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z0.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z0 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-0.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-1 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-1.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-2 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-2.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-3 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-3.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-4 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-4.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-5 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-5.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-6 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-6.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-7 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-7 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-7 I2.5 J0 F600
G1 X0 Y0 Z-7 F600
G0 X0 Y0 Z10
```

- The helix starts at the plunge height (Z2) and drops 0.5 mm in each half turn to Z-7. There is no straight plunge.
- The two flat arcs at Z-7 are the floor circle. The G1 goes off the wall to the centre before the retract.
- The same document with the Rings strategy also posts with no warning (95 lines; a G1 plunge at the centre for each of the 7 levels).
- The first `G0 X2.5 Y0` line comes before the `G0 X2.5 Y0 Z10` line: the post writes its approach first. The Rings program has the same pattern.

## Pinning tests

- `bore_helix` (motion, new):
  - `the_counterbore_is_one_helix_on_the_wall_then_a_floor_circle_and_never_a_plunge`: the issue's Ø11 x 7 counterbore with a Ø6 flat end mill at 1 mm per turn. No axial feed, no `Plunge` move, the arcs on `rc`, nine turns from 2 mm over the top to the floor, one floor circle, a feed to the centre, a retract.
  - `the_spring_pass_is_a_second_floor_circle`, `conventional_milling_turns_the_helix_clockwise`, `a_through_hole_helix_runs_on_by_the_break_through`.
  - `a_hole_one_helix_cannot_clear_is_refused_with_the_widest_it_can` (Ø12 passes, Ø14 is refused with "2.000 mm core" and "12.000 mm").
  - `a_helix_steeper_than_the_limit_is_refused_with_the_pitch_that_fits` (Ø6.5: 32.5 deg; the given pitch then passes).
  - `the_rings_strategy_is_the_default_and_keeps_its_centre_dive`.
- `bore_helical` (app, new):
  - `the_issue_counterbore_is_one_helix_and_never_plunges_into_the_block`: through `operation::generate`, with a centre-cutting and a non-centre-cutting tool. `first_solid_plunge` finds no plunge, the verifier gives no warning, 18 half-turn arcs, the floor reached. The ring ladder still dives.
  - `a_hole_too_wide_for_one_helix_is_refused_through_the_operation`.
  - `the_strategy_rides_the_project_file_and_an_older_file_reads_rings`.
  - `the_stamp_moves_when_the_strategy_changes`.
- `operation::bore_reach::tests::detect_for_a_helical_bore_skips_the_holes_one_helix_cannot_clear` (app lib).
- `egui_app::tests::bore_strategy` (ui lib, new): the Strategy row defaults to Rings, Helical shows the Spring pass check, and the Heights tab names the pitch.

## Gates

All gates ran on the final head 4bd091166. This head merges `upstream/main` at 2d98d87be and adds the `strategy` field to main's new Bore literal in `crates/motion/tests/equal_steps.rs`.

- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): 724 steps, 0 failed (113.0 min). It includes `motion suites: bore_helix`, `motion suites: equal_steps` and `app suites: bore_helical`.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` on `camcraft-geometry`, `camcraft-cl`, `camcraft-tools`, `camcraft-post`, `camcraft-sim`, `camcraft-motion`, `camcraft-app` and `camcraft-ui`: clean.
- Heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`): 240 steps (202 app heavy, 37 motion heavy, 1 build), 0 failed (63.8 min). The 6 known-fail steps (#1950, #2849) are red as expected.
- The earlier head c70e84309 had a quick gate of 687 steps and a heavy run of 231 steps, all green.

The Bore operation page, rendered by the UI test harness (`egui_kittest`) from a real Bore operation.

| | Rings | Helical |
|---|---|---|
| Passes tab | ![Passes, Rings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/3103/passes-rings.png) | ![Passes, Helical](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/3103/passes-helical.png) |

- Heights tab: the last Levels row is "Stepdown" for Rings and "Helix pitch" for Helical.

## Not exercised

- No air cut on a machine. The reporter offered in the issue to test the counterbore case.
- No GUI check by hand. The UI tests assert the rows and the combo value.
- The Bore seed stepdown is the carried stepdown (often 5 mm). A Ø11 hole with a Ø6 tool at 5 mm per turn is 17.7 deg and is refused, with the pitch to type (4.2 mm). The page does not change the stepdown when the strategy changes.
- The helix does not read the Lead-in radial engagement limit or the lead feed percentage. It reads the plunge height, the stock top and the ramp feed.
- A hole wider than twice the tool diameter is refused for the helix. The issue permits a refusal. An inner helix followed by rings is not in this PR.
- A non-centre-cutting tool helixes like any other tool. The 15 deg limit keeps the descent shallow. No tool record has a ramp limit to read.

title: feat(2d): import SVG drawings as 2D sketch profiles
body:
## What changed

The SVG reader, `camcraft_geometry::svg`, reads drawings into the DXF `Document` type. It shares sketch chaining, nesting, `SketchData`, sketch entities, and project storage with DXF import.

- Read paths, lines, polylines, polygons, rectangles, circles, and ellipses.
- Apply group transforms and references to elements in the same file.
- Keep circular arcs analytic. Flatten Beziers and other ellipses within 0.005 mm.
- Read mm, cm, in, pt, pc, and px sizes, `viewBox`, and `preserveAspectRatio`.
- Reflect Y about the page height. Use top-level group labels or IDs as layers.
- Count unsupported content, hidden content, and stylesheets as skipped. This includes stylesheets inside `<defs>`.
- Add the undoable `ImportSvg` command, the `import_svg` MCP tool, and the `cam.importSvg` script verb.
- Update the user guide and MCP reference. Record decisions in `docs/decisions/1880-svg-import.md`.

## Refusals

The reader names malformed input, unsupported units, invalid sizes, singular transforms, and exceeded import limits. A file without physical units needs the caller's unit. A sized file refuses a caller unit.

The reader also refuses inline CSS `transform` declarations and root `<svg>` transform attributes.

This review fix refuses `transform-origin` presentation attributes and inline CSS declarations by name before drawing geometry. Pins cover both sources.

## Validation on the final head

Head: `ad6709150d06595bc5b347a651702854681f457c`.
Base at gate launch: `upstream/main`, `6e641dac753020bfed49fec310237eed28448141`.
Upstream advanced during the run to `64b7377297c95d1614c93835c1a1bef18c6de174`.
The gates tested the final PR head. They did not test a trial merge.
A merge-tree check with the newer upstream head is clean.
Selection comparison against the newer base: the old and current bases have the same merge base, `6e1805bfdae52fcfea71a946d381dfbfdefc79f5`. Quick (1,067 steps) and heavy (241 steps) select identical step names and commands against both bases. The final source and selection are unchanged, so no rerun was required.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1 CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1 cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` | PASS: 1,067 steps, zero failures, 40.8 minutes |
| `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1 CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1 cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` | PASS: 241 steps, zero failures, 65.1 minutes |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | PASS in the final quick gate; all targets with `-D warnings`, including geometry, app, and six other crates |
| `app suites: example_catalog` | `app suites: example_catalog` in the final quick gate: 33 passed, 2 ignored; adaptive and edgework catalog suites: 1 passed each |
| SVG suites and other reached golden suites | SVG: 15 passed; refusals: 16 passed; visibility: 11 passed. Total: 42 passed. Reached catalog suites passed |

Pin proof:

- `svg_transform_origin_attribute_is_refused_by_name`: removing the attribute guard failed the exact pin at its assertion (exit 101); restoring the guard passed the pin (1 passed).
- `svg_inline_css_transform_origin_is_refused_by_name`: removing the inline guard failed the exact pin at its assertion (exit 101); restoring the guard passed the pin (1 passed).

Each mutation removed the relevant refusal, failed the pin, restored the refusal, and passed the pin.

An earlier seeded run failed with an infrastructure error (`E0463`) in the kernel artifact cache. A targeted repair restored the cache. The final quick gate above passed without seed artifacts.

## Goldens moved

None. The catalog suites passed. No recorded program or golden changed, so no regeneration was required.

## Not exercised

- The `import_svg` row in `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md` remains outside this fix round.
- Nested SVG viewports, stylesheet evaluation, text to outlines, and embedded images remain outside this reader's scope.

No UI source changed. Before/after screenshots do not apply.
