title: feat(waterjet): Waterjet Profile operation on a shared 2D sheet kernel
body:
## What changed

- **Shared 2D sheet kernel (`crates/motion/src/sheet/`).** The kernel code moves out of `plasma` and `wire_edm` without a change of behaviour:
  - `nest` (contour roles, inner-first cut order) and `ring` (kerf ring, walks), from `plasma`;
  - `laws` (kerf law, cover law) and `lead` (straight and arc leads), from `plasma`;
  - `arclen` (a ring by arc length), from `wire_edm::tabs`;
  - `open` (the one-sided offset of an open run), from `wire_edm::open`.

  A `Voice` keeps each refusal text word for word. Plasma and wire EDM now call the shared code.
- **Cover law.** The law now takes one span or more for each contour, and an `exempt` closure for a tab's bridge. Plasma exempts no point. The law now refuses a closed contour that has no span.
- **Waterjet generator (`crates/motion/src/waterjet/`).** `waterjet_profile` does these steps:
  - It cuts the inner contours first, with the kerf ring at kerf / 2 on the waste side.
  - It adds straight or arc leads, with the pierce in the scrap. A lead with no room is halved up to four times.
  - It pierces a tight hole at its centre when the lead has no room after the halving.
  - It cuts tabs as uncut gaps. Each stretch between two gaps gets its own pierce, lead-in and lead-out.
  - It cuts open runs on the centre line, or to the left or right of travel.
  - It can post G41/G42, and it can send arcs as chords (`Move::chords`).

  The kerf law and the cover law certify the result.
- **App.** The changes are:
  - `OpType::WaterjetProfile` (stored id 44), `Section::Waterjet` and `Family::Waterjet`. The op mounts a `ToolKind::Waterjet` nozzle only.
  - `WaterjetOp` with its command-door sanity check, `waterjet_op.rs` (seed, params, generate) and the digest bytes.
  - A `.camproj` DTO (`waterjet_profile`, additive).
  - Each exhaustive match in the app gets a waterjet arm.
  - Profile (DXF) sources are admitted. The family door has its own words: "mount a waterjet first".
  - MCP reaches the kind through the generic `add_operation` / `edit_operation`. The `add_operation` text now names waterjet.
- **UI.** The changes are:
  - `waterjet_page.rs` with these fields: kerf, compensation, direction, open-run side, send arcs as lines, sheet heights, tabs, lead shape and lengths, cut feed, pierce time, abrasive delay. It has no torch height or THC field.
  - The Waterjet ribbon section.
  - An original glyph (`assets/ui/svg/op-waterjet-profile.svg`, rasterised by `cargo xtask icons`).

## Readings

- Golden `waterjet_tabbed_plate_with_holes.cl` has 149 moves, 5 pierces and 3 holes cut before the outline. The outline is cut as two led-in stretches between 2 mm tabs.
- The existing goldens do not change. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` shows only the new file. The plasma golden `plasma_plate_with_holes.cl` stays byte-identical after the kernel move.

## Tests (pins)

Each pin was red before this change: the module and the kind did not exist, so the pins could not compile.

- motion `waterjet::tests` (9): `holes_are_cut_before_the_outline_and_every_pierce_is_in_the_waste`, `straight_leads_lay_no_arc_on_a_square_part`, `tabs_leave_uncut_gaps_and_each_stretch_is_pierced_and_led_in`, `a_tight_hole_is_pierced_at_its_centre`, `linearize_sends_every_arc_as_chords`, `an_open_run_rides_its_stated_side`, `control_compensation_records_a_comp_span_per_untabbed_contour`, `bad_input_is_refused_by_name`, `a_slot_narrower_than_the_kerf_is_refused_not_bridged`.
- app `waterjet_profile` (6): the family door, hole first, tabs, a milling tool refused, create / edit / undo / redo, and a byte-identical `.camproj` round trip.
- app `mcp_waterjet` (1): add, edit, undo, redo and generate over MCP.
- app `golden_cl::waterjet_tabbed_plate_with_holes_matches_golden`.
- ui `waterjet_ribbon_tests` (2): the section shows on a waterjet only, the tip names the waterjet, the glyph is its own, and the page has a leads tab.
- Plasma and wire EDM: all `camcraft-motion` plasma, sheet and wire tests pass, and all 34 `golden_cl` tests pass.

## Mutation results

Each mutation was applied, the pins were run, and then the code was restored (green again).

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| Inner-first order removed | red: `holes_are_cut_before_...`, `a_tight_hole_...` |
| Tabs ignored | red: `tabs_leave_uncut_gaps_...`, `bad_input_...` |
| Tight-hole rule off | red: `a_tight_hole_is_pierced_at_its_centre` |
| Linearization ignored | red: `linearize_sends_every_arc_as_chords` |
| Cover law exempts every point | red: `a_slot_narrower_than_the_kerf_is_refused_not_bridged` |
| Cover law exempts no point | red: `tabs_leave_uncut_gaps_...` (6 mm tabs) |
| Leads on the part side | red: 7 of 9 pins |

## Gate

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 422 steps ran (374 app, 44 post, 3 motion, 1 cl). The only red steps were kind-count pins that this change extends on purpose: `lathe_voice::tests::every_kind_is_work_spindle_live_tool_or_refused_by_name`, `operation::tests::stamp_follows_every_input` and `tests/ribbon.rs` (`family_is_derived_not_forked`, `the_probe_appends_its_id_and_lists_in_drilling`). I updated them to 45 kinds and the Waterjet section. Because I edited during the run, the gate marked that run VOID. `--failed` on the committed tree then ran the red step: green. The app lib suite is green (290).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib`: 1324 passed, 0 failed. The waterjet row was added to `tips_match_the_imgui_table`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: green.

- Review fix on `aded58c47` (merged with `upstream/main` `f036dddad`):
  - `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 694 steps, 1 failed. The red step is `app suites: tool_gate` (`the_refusal_names_a_fitting_catalog_entry`). Its red row is `OpType::Finish3D`: `upstream/main` (#3069) adds `Router ball nose 6 mm` before `BN-0600` in the catalog, and the tie goes to the first entry. The step is red on `upstream/main` too. The waterjet row in the same test passes.
  - `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: 237 steps, 0 failed. The lanes are `motion heavy` (37 steps), `app heavy` (199 steps) and the heavy build.
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: green.

## Not exercised

- Posting. No post serves `Kind::Waterjet` yet. The pierce time and the abrasive delay are in the path notes only. #1882 adds the CL record and the post hooks.
- `verify` and the post gate for a waterjet op. That is #1885.
- Selection of the cut data from the nozzle's recipe. This is follow-up #3047.
- The MCP skill row. The skill file is a protected path in this session. This is follow-up #3048.
- The UI page was not opened in an interactive window. The screenshots below come from the off-screen egui_kittest and wgpu render of the real shell.

## Screenshots

The images are on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch (commit `4dad162f3`, folder `pr-3058/v2/`). They come from the off-screen egui_kittest and wgpu render of the real shell on the same machine. The render code is not committed.

title: feat(post): waterjet records, CR LF, travel, programBounds and a generic waterjet post
body:
## Review fixes and final-head validation

Final head: `ca7ba50664f6d4605b96f468b17eccc6a04f5821`.

This update fixes the two findings in the latest review.

1. The engine preserves the original motion record's signed Z change on every generated chord. The waterjet post refuses that change before it writes a cutting block. Pin: `waterjet_post_refuses_a_helical_arc_in_both_arc_modes`. The test checks the named Z refusal and no cutting blocks in circular and linear modes.
2. The missing-machine test checks the CLI refusal separately from the generation log. Pin: `a_missing_default_machine_file_refuses_the_post_per_operation`. The test enables INFO logs and checks that the log names `Face1`. The selected refusal names `Setup2` and does not name `Face1`. The complete output still must name `Face2`.

Both pins pass. Each fix was removed separately. Each pin then failed with exit 101. Each restored fix passed.

Final-head results:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: GREEN. All 997 steps pass in 40.1 minutes.
- Clippy: GREEN in 78 seconds. All eight project crates pass with `--all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: RED. All 234 steps ran in 33.8 minutes. One step failed.
- The failed step is `app heavy: pocket3d_hsm`. Its failed test is `the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean` at `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs:144`.
- The test produced `(3158, 3130, 1141)`. Its Linux assertion expects `(4726, 4698, 549)`.
- All other reached motion and app heavy steps pass. The gate accepted the declared known-fail checks.
- The same test fails on the exact parent source, `b8e5e7ef21b9595a41614db04ddabf27efd5f68f`, with exit 101 and the same counts. The check restored all five changed files byte-for-byte. This update makes no unrelated change.

The PR remains a draft. No screenshots, logs, or review evidence are committed.

The sections below describe the original implementation and its historical validation. Their test counts and gate results are historical.

## What changed

- The post engine reads a `lineEnding` manifest entry. The value `"lf"` is the default. The value `"crlf"` ends each line with `\r\n`. The engine refuses any other value by name. The engine reads the entry after `onClose`, so `onOpen` can set it from a declared option.
- `machine.travel` gives the stated linear strokes `{X, Y, Z}` to scripts. Each value is `[min, max]` in mm, or `null`. The mirror now carries the `travel` of a linear axis. The raw door reads a vendor tree through `parse_mch`.
- The engine publishes `programBounds` before `onOpen`. It is the XY box of the cutting records, or `null`. Arcs count at the quarter points that they pass (`machine::move_extremes`). Rapids do not count.
- New stream records `WATERJET [ABRASIVE] [DWELL<ms>] [LAG<ms>]` and `JET ON C<id> <ROLE>` / `JET OFF C<id>`. The cl types are `cl::WaterjetCut` and `cl::JetSpan` (`crates/cl/src/cl/jet.rs`). The reader takes the `.cnc` form and the `.cl` comment form.
- The new hooks `onJetOn` / `onJetOff` fire under a `JetLaw` (`cnc_jet.rs`). The law refuses by name: a jet with no header, an ON while a jet is on, a rapid while a jet is on, and a jet that stays on. It shares no state with the plasma `TorchLaw`.
- `linearizeArcs = true` posts each arc as chords through `onLinear`, at `chordTolerance` mm (0.01 when unstated). The engine refuses a bad tolerance by name. The chords come from `cl::Move::segments3`. The last chord ends on the arc's end point. All chord lines map to the arc record.
- A WCS flip on a waterjet section is refused by name, the same as for plasma.
- New post `assets/posts/waterjet-iso.cps` (generic ISO abrasive waterjet). It writes `G20`/`G21`, `G90 G94 G17 G40`, a work offset, and `G0`/`G1`/`G2`/`G3` (or G1 chords). It writes XY only. Each contour gets: water on, `G4` valve lag, abrasive on, `G4` pierce dwell, the cut, abrasive off, water off. The four M numbers, the G4 word form, the arc form and the line ending are declared options. The default M numbers (M10/M11, M12/M13) are placeholders, and the post header says so.
- The post refuses by name: an rpm (S, G95), a surface speed (G96), coolant, a section with no `WATERJET` header, a machine not declared `kind: waterjet`, a rotary, a cycle, a Z cutting move, and a cut outside the stated `machine.travel`.
- Docs: `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md` (records, properties, "Waterjet records") and `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` (hooks, sheet-cutting seams, the waterjet post).
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1882-waterjet-post.md`.

## Cause

This is new work for #1882. The engine wrote only `\n` lines. It did not publish linear travel or a cut box. It had no waterjet records or jet hooks, and no waterjet post was available.

## Tests

Pins (all red on the upstream sources, 17 of 17):

- `crates/post/tests/waterjet_engine.rs` (12 tests): `line_ending_crlf_ends_every_line_with_cr_lf`, `line_ending_other_words_are_refused_by_name`, `program_bounds_box_the_cut_moves_and_skip_rapids`, `machine_travel_publishes_the_linear_strokes`, `machine_travel_rides_the_mirror_and_the_raw_file`, `linearize_arcs_posts_chords_ending_on_the_arc_end`, `linearize_arcs_refuses_a_bad_tolerance_by_name`, `waterjet_records_fire_the_jet_hooks_with_their_properties`, `waterjet_records_round_trip_in_both_spellings`, `waterjet_law_refuses_what_the_stream_cannot_mean`, `waterjet_header_and_open_jet_end_with_their_section`, `waterjet_section_under_a_flipped_wcs_is_refused_by_name`.
- `crates/post/tests/waterjet_iso_post.rs` (7 tests): the goldens `plate.nc` (mm, G2/G3) and `plate_inch_chords.nc` (inch, G1 chords, CR LF, `G4 P` ms, custom M numbers), and the refusals for spindle words, a section that is not a waterjet cut, a machine that is not a waterjet, travel, a Z cut, a dry cut and a cycle.
- `crates/post/tests/script_waterjet_iso.rs`: the recorded-stream suite (11 refusal goldens; no recorded stream is a waterjet cut).
- `crates/cl/src/cl/jet.rs` unit tests: line round trip, bad words, span sanity.

Mutation checks (one guard changed, its pin run, the guard put back): 21 of 21 red. The guards: the CR LF join, the `lineEnding` refusal, the bounds publish, the rapid skip, the arc quarter points, the travel in props, the travel in the mirror, the chord branch, the tolerance check, the jet-hook check, the jet rapid law, the jet section end, the jet fire, the WCS-flip refusal, the post rpm, CSS, header, kind, travel and Z refusals, and the order abrasive off before water off.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green: 996 steps, 0 failed (wall 30.5 min; the `cl` change reaches each dependent crate). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

Branch history: the first commit was squashed onto a newer main by mistake, so it reverted nine files of the Tormach lathe G76 work (#2952). The second commit restores them from main. The net diff against main has only the #1882 files (34 files). The four new Tormach lathe test binaries pass on the combined tree. The quick gate ran on the base `768fe23f0`, before that main change; main's change since then touches none of the files of this PR.

## Goldens moved

title: feat(2d): rest machining on the 2D Adaptive from the previous operations
body:
Stacked on #2822 (merge #2822 first).

This PR is a `feat`: it adds a parameter group. The default (off) does not change an output.

## What changed

The 2D Adaptive operation has the rest machining group.
With the group on, the operation cuts only what the earlier operations of the same setup left.

- `OpParams::Adaptive2D` has the field `rest: Option<RestParams>`. `None` is off and is the default.
- `machining2d::rest_adaptive_previous` (new, motion crate) reads the stock of the previous operations with `rest_stock_from_columns` (#2033). It gives that stock to the rest Adaptive planner `rest_adaptive` (#2031).
- Each plunge stands where that stock proves the whole cutter clear. The planner holds the optimal load on the material that stands.
- `adaptive::rest_levels` (new) gives the cut depths of the rest planner. The stock is read at exactly those depths.
- The group rides the existing `EditOperationParams` command (undo and redo), the project key `rest` of the 2D Adaptive and the MCP `edit_operation` parameter. A file without the key reads as off.
- The stamp writes byte `0xD9` and the allowance when the group is on. An operation without the group keeps its stamp.

Refused by name, at the edit and again at generation:

- An entered previous tool (`REST_ADAPTIVE_ENTERED`). An entered diameter does not prove where material is absent (#2031). The 2D Pocket keeps that mode.
- The Trochoidal method, arc turns, a tilt. The rest planner does not read them, so they are not dropped silently.
- A negative or non-finite allowance.

Refused by name at generation:

- An earlier operation with no toolpath, a stale toolpath, or a suppressed cut (the refusals of #2033).
- No stock ahead (`REST_ADAPTIVE_NO_STOCK`). The 2D Pocket cuts the whole pocket in this case. The 2D Adaptive does not, because the rest planner cannot enter a full pocket.
- A roughing pass that stops above the floor: "rest Adaptive has no entry with proved clearance".

## Cause

The rest Adaptive planner (#2031) had no door from an operation.
The retired Adaptive strategy of the 2D Pocket was its only possible caller (#2253).
The 2D Adaptive operation had no rest parameter and no producer of the proved stock.

## Two findings

- The column reading of #2033 leaves a band along each wall that an earlier tool cut to. On a 0.1 mm grid the band is 0.14 mm thick. With the film of #2033 (one cell diagonal) the planner read the band as rest material and refused the fixture ("would reach 23 passes by a retract"). The film is now `cell * (1 + sqrt 2)`. The band still stands for each plunge and each load reading. No pass is planned for it. The path note states the film.
- An allowance of 0.6 mm grew that band to 0.74 mm, and the planner found no entry. The allowance now grows only material that is thicker than the film. It never makes the standing material smaller.

## Tests

Red before the change: the pins use the new field and the new function, so they do not compile on unchanged code. The mutation results are the proof for each guard.

Pins, all new:

- `crates/app/tests/rest_adaptive_op.rs` (6 tests):
  - `the_rest_adaptive_pass_cuts_what_the_simulated_roughing_pass_left`: the real job (60 x 40 pocket, 3 mm corners, 12 mm roughing tool, 4 mm rest tool) against an independent simulation of the roughing pass. Each standing column is cut. No plunge goes down a column that the roughing pass left under the cutter. No rapid is below the top of the stock, but a straight lift. Each feed stays at a corner.
  - `a_stock_that_does_not_prove_an_entry_is_refused_by_name`
  - `what_the_rest_planner_does_not_read_is_refused_by_name_at_the_edit`
  - `a_document_past_the_door_is_refused_at_generation`
  - `the_group_is_an_undoable_edit_a_project_file_key_and_moves_the_stamp`
  - `mcp_sets_the_group_refuses_the_entered_tool_undoes_and_the_project_keeps_it`
- `crates/app/src/operation/rest_op_tests.rs`: `the_adaptive_rest_group_moves_the_stamp`, `the_adaptive_rest_group_refuses_bad_values_without_a_tool`.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/rest_prior_adaptive_tests.rs` (lib): `each_guard_is_pinned_and_its_removal_fails_the_pin`, `the_allowance_never_makes_the_standing_material_smaller`, `bad_rest_values_are_refused_by_name`.
- `crates/motion/tests/rest_adaptive/main.rs`: `the_column_stock_of_the_previous_operations_plans_the_rest_adaptive_pass` (the laws of #2031 on the column stock: verifier, plunges, rapids, load, coverage), `the_previous_operations_planner_refuses_what_it_cannot_prove`.

Mutations (one guard removed, its pin run, then restored and green):

| Guard removed | Pin | Mutant |
|---|---|---|
| generate: the rest planner is called | `the_rest_adaptive_pass_cuts_...` | red |
| generate: the refusals stand at generation | `a_document_past_the_door_...` | red |
| `rest_op`: entered tool refused | `what_the_rest_planner_does_not_read_...` | red |
| `rest_op`: Trochoidal refused | same | red |
| `rest_op`: arc turns refused | same | red |
| `rest_op`: tilt refused | same | red |
| `rest_op`: bad values refused without a tool | `the_adaptive_rest_group_refuses_bad_values_without_a_tool` | red |
| `rest_op`: the 2D Adaptive reads the previous operations (job stock, earlier-operation refusals) | `a_stock_that_does_not_prove_an_entry_...` | red |
| `params`: stamp byte `0xD9` | `the_adaptive_rest_group_moves_the_stamp` | red |

| project: the key is written | `the_group_is_an_undoable_edit_...` | red |

| motion: entered mode refused (`Guards::source`) | `each_guard_is_pinned_...` | red |
| motion: no stock refused (`Guards::stock`) | same | red |

The three motion guards have a switch in the code (`rest_prior_adaptive::Guards`), and the unit test turns each off.

title: fix(geometry): order sheet cuts before material release
body:
Stacked on #2808 (merge #2808 first)

## What changed

Add `camcraft_geometry::nesting::cut_order` for one placed sheet.
Build a global containment forest for closed loops and open chains.
Resolve closed `Auto` sides by depth parity and open `Auto` sides to `OnLine`.
Traverse the forest iteratively. Sort siblings by enclosed area, then stable ID.
Schedule marking, internal, rough profile, and final breakthrough phases.
Use an explicit `release_phase` to distinguish blind pockets from through cuts.
Refuse invalid geometry, side requests, incomplete schedules, and cuts after material release.
Report circular-tool corner limits without changing the picked geometry.

## Cause

The geometry crate lacked one cut order across a nested sheet.
An enclosing hole can free a smaller part before that part's cuts finish.
Independent operation orders cannot enforce that sheet relationship.

## Tests

The initial pinning build failed on unchanged upstream base `f3b0e1955` with `E0432` because the planner API was absent.
The tested stacked base is parent commit `1947b6b6c30d214baf3db2072f95ed51ccb2dae3` from #2808.

- `sheet_pass_phases_keep_marking_first_and_breakthrough_last`

- `sheet_order_validator_refuses_released_ancestors_missing_and_extra_passes`

- `sheet_order_validator_names_unrequested_and_duplicate_open_passes`
- `sheet_refuses_a_later_pass_after_the_same_contour_releases`
- `sheet_blind_pocket_pass_keeps_material_until_final_breakthrough`
- `sheet_refuses_invalid_release_phase_requests`
- `sheet_open_chain_sides_resolve_and_invalid_sides_name_the_chain`
- `sheet_refuses_invalid_width_ids_and_pass_requests`
- `sheet_refuses_degenerate_self_crossing_and_retraced_geometry`
- `sheet_refuses_area_accumulation_overflow_by_name`
- `sheet_refuses_crossing_or_touching_contours_and_boundary_crossing_chains`
- `sheet_crossing_open_features_keep_the_same_containing_parent`

- `sheet_open_side_corner_limits_follow_the_directed_cut_side`

The mutations covered:

- Width, duplicate IDs, pass requests, release requests, mandatory breakthrough release, and open/closed side requests.
- Minimum vertices, finite coordinates, coordinate bounds, zero-length segments, open closure, retracing, self-crossing, boundary crossing, and area overflow.
- Unknown cuts, extra or duplicate passes, global phase order, released material, and missing passes.

The area mutation used wrapping addition. Only the new overflow pin failed; the other 16 pins passed.
The spiral fixture checks positive and negative overflow in a valid 642-vertex loop.
Copying the upstream nesting entry back failed with `E0432`. Restoring the stacked entry passed all 17 pins.

This head merges `upstream/main` into the branch. The merge has no conflicts and no hand edits (class SAME).
The merge gives the branch the light tier. The source of the PR is not changed.

title: fix(sinker): judge body electrodes against cavity outlines
body:
## What changed

It adds `cavity_outline` to Sinker Burn parameters.
The points use coordinates relative to the burn point.
The project file, operation digest and MCP tools carry the outline.
An empty outline keeps the previous extent law.

The size law compares the electrode with inward cavity wall offsets.
It permits the derived diamond finish electrode.
It still refuses an oversized electrode by name.
It also refuses malformed outlines, contradictory dimensions and an incomplete finish.
Command creation checks the outline and its stated dimensions.
Generation repeats the bounds checks.
The existing scalar law keeps the floor and condition checks.

The MCP schema declares an optional array with a `null` default.
The electrode reply supplies an array for a body and `null` for a rectangle.
A `null` params patch clears the outline.
The independent stock verdict still checks the actual burn.
Two legacy-extent tests generate box burns and check the corner gouges.

The undercut stock check uses exact disc-polygon intersection.
It blocks a plunge or retract when the cutter head meets a stock corner.
The lollipop profile draws the full ball united with the neck.
The record law now refuses a lollipop neck that ends below the ball top.
The refusal names the lollipop, neck length and required ball height.
The shortest accepted stack includes the whole ball.
The drawn-cutter length remains the stated flute length plus neck length.

## UI screenshots

These inherited parent renders use the headless `ShellUi` (`1440x960` WGPU).
The before views show upstream `5ed5b7fe2`.
The after views come from parent PR #2714.
The pictured UI files are unchanged in #2836.
The images are stored only on `mkinney/Camcraft` branch `pr-screenshots`, at commit `0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86`:

| View | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Tool editor (`DT-20-60` dovetail cutter) | ![Tool editor before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86/2714/tool-editor-before.png) | ![Tool editor after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86/2714/tool-editor-after.png) |
| Slot Undercut page (`TSlot` in milling setup) | ![Slot Undercut before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86/2714/slot-undercut-before.png) | ![Slot Undercut after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86/2714/slot-undercut-after.png) |

## Cause

The previous law judged X and Y extents.
An inward offset moves a sharp diamond corner farther than the condition's undersize.
The correct finish electrode then failed the extent check.
The original pin reported a burned X extent of `19.962` for a `20.000` cavity.

## Tests

The original pin failed before the production change:

- `a_diamond_cavity_finish_is_generated_and_judged_clean`

The MCP pin covers schema discovery, translated outlines, generation, null clearing and early refusals:

The ten motion pins pass:

- `a_vector_orbit_does_not_certify_angled_walls`

Each mutation failed its pin with the old code or the guard removed.

title: feat(2d): arc turns and their radius on Face, 2D Contour and Slot
body:
## What changed

Face, 2D Contour and Slot have the arc turns option with a corner arc radius. The parameters are `blend_turns` and `blend_radius`, the same as on 2D Pocket, 2D Adaptive and 2D Offset (#1733).

All three kinds can round their corners safely. No kind is left out.

- **2D Contour** had `blend_turns`. It gets `blend_radius`. No radius is the tool radius, as before.
- **Face** had `blend_turns`. It gets `blend_radius`. No radius is the semicircle of half the row spacing, as before. A smaller radius gives two quarter arcs with a straight step between them. The step is one radius outside the overrun line, away from the footprint. With a radius, rows spaced wider than the tool diameter turn on arcs too.
- **Slot** gets `blend_turns` and `blend_radius`. Each row-end corner of the serpentine pass turns on one tangent arc. No radius is the tool radius. The new module is `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slot_turns.rs`.

The parameter door (`sane.rs`) refuses a radius below 0.01 mm on the three kinds. The generators refuse a radius larger than the tool radius, with the text of `corner_arc_radius`. The project file writes the keys only when they are set. The cache digest reads the radius only when the option is on.

The operation pages show the radius rows when the option is on. The Face page names its default "Arc radius = half the row spacing".

MCP: `edit_operation` sets the two fields through `EditOperationParams`. No new command and no new tool are necessary.

The type is `feat`, because the change adds parameters. The task template gave `fix`.

## Cause

The fix for #1733 gave the radius to the three pocket kinds only. Face and 2D Contour had the option without a radius. Slot did not have the option.

## Which corners turn, and why no arc cuts past the wall

- 2D Contour: only a corner that turns toward the air gets an arc. This is the law of `fillet.rs`, and it did not change. A corner that turns toward the part stays sharp, and the notes name it. A convex outside corner is such a corner, so an arc cannot leave material there.
- Face: each point of a turn is on or outside the overrun line, one tool radius from the footprint. The turn reaches one radius past that line at most.
- Slot: the pass is in the cutter-center stadium, which is convex. A fillet is inside the triangle of its corner and its two tangent points, and that triangle is inside the stadium. `fillet_corners` proves each triangle again and keeps a corner sharp if it cannot prove it. An arc leaves corner rest at the round end of the slot. The note states the largest rest.

## Tests

Pins in `crates/motion/tests/arc_turn_kinds.rs` (13 tests):

- `face_row_ends_turn_on_tangent_arcs_of_the_given_radius`
- `a_face_turn_never_exceeds_the_radius_when_the_straight_step_is_short` (review fix)
- `no_face_arc_turn_cuts_past_the_overrun_line`
- `a_face_radius_past_half_the_row_spacing_turns_on_the_semicircle`
- `a_face_radius_rounds_rows_spaced_wider_than_the_tool`
- `the_face_door_refuses_a_radius_no_control_can_cut_and_reads_none_when_off`
- `contour_corners_turn_on_tangent_arcs_of_the_given_radius`
- `no_contour_arc_turn_cuts_past_the_wall`
- `no_contour_radius_is_the_tool_radius_and_the_door_refuses_by_name`
- `slot_row_ends_turn_on_tangent_arcs_of_the_given_radius`
- `no_slot_arc_turn_cuts_past_the_wall`
- `no_slot_radius_is_the_tool_radius_and_the_door_refuses_by_name`
- `a_one_row_slot_has_no_corner_and_says_so`

Pins in `crates/app/tests/arc_turn_kinds.rs` (6 tests):

- `face_contour_and_slot_take_arc_turns_and_a_radius_through_edit_operation_and_undo`
- `a_radius_no_control_can_cut_is_refused_by_name_on_each_kind`
- `the_project_file_keeps_the_radius_and_a_default_file_has_no_key`
- `generation_cuts_the_face_and_the_slot_turns_at_the_radius_asked`
- `generation_refuses_a_radius_past_the_tool_radius_by_name_on_each_kind`
- `the_stamp_tells_a_radius_from_none_and_a_default_op_keeps_its_stamp`

Two unit tests in `blend.rs`: `a_user_radius_turns_on_corner_arcs_where_the_stride_has_room` and `a_short_step_never_turns_on_an_arc_larger_than_the_radius` (review fix). Two unit tests there changed with the plan type (`bool` became `Option<Turn>`).

Red before the change: yes. On the unchanged code the motion pin does not compile, because `FaceParams`, `ContourParams` and `SlotParams` have no such fields (`error[E0560]`).

Mutation results. Each mutation put one guard back to the old behaviour. Each pin went red, and green again after the restore.

| Mutation | Pin | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Contour reads the tool radius, not `blend_radius` | `contour_corners_turn_on_tangent_arcs_of_the_given_radius` | red |
| Contour has no radius door | `no_contour_radius_is_the_tool_radius_and_the_door_refuses_by_name` | red |

| `sane.rs` door without the three kinds | `a_radius_no_control_can_cut_is_refused_by_name_on_each_kind` | red |
| `generate.rs` drops the Face radius | `generation_cuts_the_face_and_the_slot_turns_at_the_radius_asked` | red |
| `generate.rs` drops the Slot option | `generation_cuts_the_face_and_the_slot_turns_at_the_radius_asked` | red |
| `generate.rs` drops the Contour radius | `generation_refuses_a_radius_past_the_tool_radius_by_name_on_each_kind` | red |
| Slot digest without the option | `the_stamp_tells_a_radius_from_none_and_a_default_op_keeps_its_stamp` | red |
| Face digest without the radius | `the_stamp_tells_a_radius_from_none_and_a_default_op_keeps_its_stamp` | red |
| Contour digest without the radius | `the_stamp_tells_a_radius_from_none_and_a_default_op_keeps_its_stamp` | red |
| Slot project file drops the option on save | `the_project_file_keeps_the_radius_and_a_default_file_has_no_key` | red |
| Face takes the semicircle when half the spacing is less than 0.005 mm past the radius (review fix) | `a_face_turn_never_exceeds_the_radius_when_the_straight_step_is_short`, `blend::law::a_short_step_never_turns_on_an_arc_larger_than_the_radius` | red (`actual radii: [0.012500000000000178]` for 0.01 mm) |

### Review fix: the Face radius bound

`corner_turn` in `blend.rs` gave the semicircle when half the row spacing was less than 0.005 mm past the radius. That semicircle is larger than the radius. Now:

- If half the spacing is not more than the radius (1e-9 mm float margin), the turn is the semicircle, as before. Its radius is not larger than the requested radius.
- If half the spacing is more than the radius by 0.005 mm or less, the turn uses two corner arcs. Their radius is half the spacing minus 0.005 mm, which is less than the requested radius. The straight step stays 0.01 mm.
- If that radius is below 0.01 mm, the turn stays sharp. The status line counts it as the `Tiny` refusal ("row spacing below the 0.020 mm arc resolution").

Pins: `crates/motion/tests/arc_turn_kinds.rs::a_face_turn_never_exceeds_the_radius_when_the_straight_step_is_short` (the reviewer's 60 x 10.025 mm case and three other spacings), and the unit test `blend::law::a_short_step_never_turns_on_an_arc_larger_than_the_radius`.

### Review fix: the exhaustive test literals

The latest review found missing required fields in nine exhaustive test literals from main. The branch now includes a merge of upstream main `aa4c785dbd53715f1d811524dc99c688b9380cba`.

- Face literals have `blend_radius: None` in `chamfer_partly_bevelled`, `first_traverse`, `first_traverse_table`, `setup_move_order`, `stock_copy_hole`, `vouch_fidelity` and `vouch_fidelity_mcp`.
- Slot literals have `blend_turns: false` and `blend_radius: None` in `tilt_basis0_edited_file` and `tilt_stock_cap`.
- Current main adds the same missing Face default in `first_traverse_mill_turn` and `model_fidelity_wide`. These literals have `blend_radius: None` too.

- Current main also adds a Contour literal and a Slot literal in `crates/motion/tests/equal_steps.rs`. The Contour literal has `blend_radius: None`. The Slot literal has `blend_turns: false` and `blend_radius: None`.

- The test helper in `crates/app/src/operation/first_traverse.rs` also has `blend_radius: None`. Its pin is `operation::first_traverse::tests::a_mill_turn_judges_its_milling_kinds_in_the_mill_order`.

- The Contour literal in `crates/app/tests/equal_steps.rs` has `blend_radius: None`. Its pin is `equal_steps::edit_sets_equal_steps_and_undo_restores_the_remainder_ladder`.

The fix adds 18 default-field lines in fourteen files. All changed literals are in tests. It changes no runtime source logic.

Runtime pins: eleven app suites passed 47 tests. Motion `equal_steps` passed 13 tests. The app first-traverse unit pin passed one test. App `equal_steps` passed six tests.

Mutation: removing the added defaults gave compiler error `E0063` in the affected literals. Restoring the defaults made all fourteen affected suites compile and pass.

Final head: `4adba68fd814090bac6f28bc2acd4e0eb4675200`

Quick gate: 761 steps passed on final head `4adba68fd814090bac6f28bc2acd4e0eb4675200`, against upstream main `aa4c785dbd53715f1d811524dc99c688b9380cba`. The first run passed all 123 motion steps. The app build then stopped on a stale local `camcraft_kernel` artifact (`E0463`) after the check profile changed. After rebuilding that local artifact, `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main --only app --only ui` passed all 638 selected steps, with 0 failed, in 38.6 minutes. These two runs cover the quick plan: 7,028 tests passed, 0 failed and 115 ignored. No source change was needed for the artifact failure.

Heavy lanes: `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` passed on final head `4adba68fd814090bac6f28bc2acd4e0eb4675200`: 237 steps, 0 failed, in 44.3 minutes. The reached motion and app heavy lanes ran. The lanes ran 100 passing tests and six expected failures: three for #1950 and three for #2849. There were 0 unexpected failures. Motion had 38 steps and 57 passing tests. App had 198 steps and 43 passing tests. The shared build was one step.

Clippy: `cargo clippy -j 16 -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed in 40.41 seconds.

The results above are for the old head `4adba68fd`. The results for the current head are in the next section.

### Review fix: the merge conflicts with main

The branch now includes a merge of upstream main `6ffa808ae`. Four files had conflicts. Each resolution keeps the two sides:

- `crates/app/tests/first_router_part.rs`, `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/guide_images.rs` and `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/guide_projects.rs`: the Contour literals keep `blend_radius` from this PR and `chain_overrides` from main.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/mod.rs`: `mod slot_turns;` from this PR and `mod undercut;` from main both stay.

Main added literals that do not have the new fields. These got the defaults:

- `blend_radius: None` in `crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_lead.rs`, `crates/app/tests/klartext_builtin.rs` (two literals) and `crates/app/tests/first_traverse_table_tilt.rs`.
- `blend_turns: false` and `blend_radius: None` in the Slot literal of `crates/app/tests/posting_rotaries_first.rs`.
- The Contour literal of this PR's `crates/app/tests/arc_turn_kinds.rs` got `chain_overrides: Vec::new()`.

After the merge, `crates/app/src/operation/params.rs` had 402 lines, and `params_files_stay_under_the_line_law` failed. Commit `8716a45fd` moves the Face and Contour radius writes into `digest::write_blend_radius`. The digest bytes do not change. The file now has 392 lines.

The merged `sane.rs`, `generate.rs`, `params_impl.rs` and `first_traverse.rs` keep each guard of main. This PR only adds its fields there.

Pins and mutations:

- Without `blend_radius` in `contour_tab_lead` or `chain_overrides` in `first_router_part`, the build gave `E0063`. After the restore, both compiled and passed.
- With `write_blend_radius` made to ignore the radius, `the_stamp_tells_a_radius_from_none_and_a_default_op_keeps_its_stamp` failed. After the restore, it passed.
- `params_files_stay_under_the_line_law` failed on the merge commit and passes on the final head.

Final head: `8716a45fd68172e916d76b7e554be37ae976bab9`

Quick gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the final head: 780 steps, 0 failed, 45.8 minutes.

Heavy lanes: `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` on the final head: 240 steps, 0 failed, 30.4 minutes. The reached motion and app heavy lanes ran. Six known-fail checks gave the expected red: three for #1950 and three for #2849.

Clippy: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed on the final head.

### Review fix: the new Contour and Slot literals

The latest review found two new exhaustive literals from main without the required defaults. The branch includes upstream main `6e1805bfdae52fcfea71a946d381dfbfdefc79f5`. Merge commit `e79d3248ec63dde01891fd4ca165098d6026cd62` has no conflicts.

- `crates/app/tests/contour_none_lead.rs` has `blend_radius: None` on Contour.
- `crates/app/tests/index_swing_offset_line.rs` has `blend_turns: false` and `blend_radius: None` on Slot.

These are the only fix edits: three field lines in two test files. The existing exhaustive literals pin the required fields.

Mutation checks:

- Removing the Contour default gave `E0063` at `contour_none_lead.rs:33`. Restoring it made all four suite tests pass.
- Removing the Slot defaults gave `E0063` at `index_swing_offset_line.rs:56`. Restoring them made all three suite tests pass.

Final head: `9a5433633e9efdd4133f31074a189eafa9a79361`.

Quick gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed on the final head against upstream main `6e1805bfdae52fcfea71a946d381dfbfdefc79f5`: 786 steps, 0 failed, 71.9 minutes. Total: 7,186 tests passed and 117 were ignored.

The reached motion and app heavy lanes ran 102 passing tests: 59 motion tests and 43 app tests. Six known-fail checks gave the expected failures: three for #1950 and three for #2849. The gate accepted these results.

### Review fix: the Slot conflict with main (#2906 wall lap)

The branch now includes a merge of upstream main `a2c35e0eb`. Merge commit `22f3ffb98` resolves one conflict in `slot()` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slots.rs`. The two behaviors stay:

- The #1759 arc turns round the serpentine rows only. `rows` is a copy of the pass before the lap points join it.
- The #2906 wall lap follows the rows in the same walk. The new helper `slot_turns::with_lap` puts the rounded walk (or the straight rows, when nothing rounds) first, then the lap.
- A fillet does not move the end of a walk. Thus the rounded rows end on the tangent point where the lap starts.

Commit `d80eccfab` updates the app pin: the sharp Slot pass now has the lap's cap arcs.

Pins:

- `crates/motion/tests/slot_round_ends.rs::wide_slot_with_arc_turns_still_cuts_its_round_ends` (new). With arc turns on, climb and conventional, 10 mm and 20 mm wide: no crossing, no center outside the stadium, and no more than 0.01 mm left on the wall.
- `crates/motion/tests/arc_turn_kinds.rs::slot_row_ends_turn_on_tangent_arcs_of_the_given_radius`. The sharp pass has only cap arcs, and the rounded pass keeps the same count of lap arcs.
- `crates/app/tests/arc_turn_kinds.rs::generation_cuts_the_face_and_the_slot_turns_at_the_radius_asked`. Lap arcs and turn arcs are counted apart. The lap is the same with arc turns off and on.

Mutation: `with_lap` returned the rounded walk without the lap. All three pins went red. The round-ends pin gave "1.290 mm left on the wall". The app pin gave "the arc turns lost the wall lap". After the restore, all three passed.

title: feat(ui): "Entry positions (pre-drilled)" group on the 2D Pocket page (#1449, slice 2)
body:
Second slice of #1449. This PR does not close the issue: see "Not exercised".

## What changed

- The 2D Pocket page has a new group, "Entry positions (pre-drilled)", on the `Lead in / Lead out` tab. It is below "Horizontal arc entry".
- The group has one header switch. The switch writes `links.approach.predrilled` into the page draft.
- Apply commits the draft through `EditOperationParams`. Undo and redo restore the flag.
- The open group shows one line. The line says where the holes come from, when a hole is used, and that each other level keeps the asked entry.
- When rest machining is on in the draft, the group also shows `REST_PREDRILLED`. That is the refusal that Apply gives.
- The pages of the other kinds do not show the group. Those kinds refuse the flag (`PREDRILLED_POCKET_ONLY`).

Files:

- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/predrilled_page.rs` (new, 34 lines): the group.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/predrilled_page_tests.rs` (new): the structural tests.

- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/mod.rs`: two `mod` lines.
- `docs/decisions/1449-predrilled-entry-group.md`: the decision entry.

## Cause

Slice 1 (#1493) added the flag for MCP and for project files only. The page had no control for it. The issue comment of 2026-11-13 lists the UI group and its structural test as owed.

All three tests are in `camcraft-ui`, under `egui_app::predrilled_page_tests`:

The branch includes `upstream/main` at `35940da16955dd450eccf9a7bc61471f7f6cdafa` through a clean merge. The final quick and heavy gates used current `upstream/main` at `74ea8988d800f00d41547ec9d292077d2bc3ddc5`. The later base commit changes the Mach3 post only.

title: feat(sim): step the simulation to the next or the previous operation
body: ## What changed The simulation transport bar has two new buttons, **Previous op** and **Next op**, between Stop and the slider. Page Up and Page Down do the same steps. - **Next op** moves the playhead to the start of the next operation in program order, and pauses the playback. - **Previous op** moves to the start of the current operation. A second press moves to the start of the one before it. - The readout already names the current operation (`Contour1 · RAPID · ...`). After a step it names the new operation. - **Next** is disabled in the last operation. **Previous** is disabled at the start of the first operation. Both are disabled while the stock removal is calculated, as the slider is (#2611). - The tips (and the AccessKit descriptions) say what each step does, name the target operation and name the key. - A step across a setup boundary, a tool change or a WCS change is the same step. An operation with no toolpath is not on the timeline, so it is no stop. - The user guide (`guide/operations` "Checking") describes the two steps. The lookup is on `sim::Script` in `camcraft-sim` (`crates/sim/src/sim_steps.rs`: `op_starts`, `next_op_start`, `prev_op_start`, `op_starting_at`), so the stand-alone simulator (#2587) can use the same steps. The UI part is `crates/ui/src/egui_app/sim_steps.rs`; `shell.rs` gets one call. An operation starts at its first segment on the timeline (the connector rapid, when there is one). At that position all moves of the earlier operations are complete. A step is a scrub to that time, so the stock follows the playhead as for a scrub. Decision record: `docs/decisions/2608-sim-op-step.md`. ## Screenshots Headless render at 2x, dark theme, two operations, playhead at 1.0 s. Before (`main`): After (this PR): ## Pinning tests - `crates/sim/tests/sim_op_steps.rs` (8 tests): the value of each start from the segments (`cum[k]` of the last segment of the operation before); the kept `OpStarts` answer as the `Script` lookups; the starts in program order; next from inside operation 1 gives the start of operation 2; previous goes to the current start, then to the one before; no step past the first or the last operation; an operation with no moves is no stop; a non-finite playhead. - `crates/app/tests/sim_op_step_stock.rs` (2 tests): "next" from inside operation 1 (the next operation has another tool) gives the stock after every move of operation 1, the same picture as playback move by move; an operation with no toolpath is no stop, and the stock holds before it as in plain playback (#2280). - `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/sim_op_steps.rs` (7 tests): a still frame walks no segment (the kept starts are the same `Arc`), and a document change walks the new timeline; click and keys move the playhead and pause; enabled state at the first and the last operation and while held; the tips and the AccessKit description; the shell transport has the steps and the readout names the operation. ## Readings - `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 13 steps, 12 green. The red step is `ui suites: lib`, with four frame-cost tests that fail the same way on clean `main` at 6df70dfc5 ("the area preview is filled"). I filed #2762 for them. Each other `ui --lib` test passes. - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. ## Not exercised - No windowed run. The screenshots are headless. - The steps do not select the operation in the browser. The decision record gives the reason. - No run on Linux or macOS. MCP: no new command. The playhead is view state, not a document command. ## Heavy lanes `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` on the final head 7cdb8b8d9 (#2568). The change in `crates/sim` reaches each heavy target of `motion` and `app`. - Lanes that ran: `motion heavy` (34 steps, each target) and `app heavy` (199 steps, each target), after one release build. 234 steps in total. Wall time 40.3 min, on Windows x86_64. - Result: 233 steps ok, 1 failed. - The failed step is `app heavy: pocket3d_hsm`, test `the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean`. It gets the triple (3158, 3130, 1141), the Windows triple of the bore. This PR does not cause it: the branch base does not have the Windows pin of upstream commit 01e74d74c ("pin Windows x86_64 bore counts for the solidcore mesh"). The same test with the same triple is red on `main` at acd5b02d3 on this machine. The merge of `main` at the cut brings the pin. This PR changes no adaptive or pocket code. - The known-fail steps are red as expected: #1950 (2 steps in `motion heavy`, 1 in `app heavy`), #2845 and #2849. - The earlier run on 235201581: 217 steps, all ok. Changelog: The simulation has Previous op and Next op steps (Page Up / Page Down) that pause at the start of an operation with the stock that the earlier operations leave (#2608) Fixes #2608 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

body:
Replaces #2640 with the same Hurco commit (`4cd8bdae2`, cherry-picked unchanged) on a branch straight off `main`. #2640 was stacked on the Grbl post draft #2506, so it could not merge before #2506; this one does not need it.

## Latest review fixes

Head: `ed04216dc468f9880dea0651c813b5762c401488`.

- Finding 1: Cancel active cycles before travel. Seat each hole at the section hop before descent to R. Refuse missing hops.

No built-in post processor or machine definition existed for Hurco WinMax 3-axis NC/ISO (ISNC) mills.
